title: Strong Coupling In A Three-mode Superconducting-spin Hybrid Quantum System
authors: Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, And Johannes Majer
abstract:
Author(s): Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, and Johannes Majer

We demonstrate strong coupling in a solid-state hybrid quantum system comprising a fixed-frequency coplanar-waveguide resonator, a superconducting transmon qubit, and an ensemble of nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond. Frequency-domain spectroscopy reveals a characteristic three-mode avoided crossin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023343] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates strong coupling in a three-mode hybrid system of a superconducting resonator, transmon qubit, and NV center ensemble.
motivation: Hybrid quantum systems combining superconducting circuits and spin ensembles are promising for quantum information processing, but achieving strong coupling in multi-mode configurations is challenging.
method: Frequency-domain spectroscopy is used to observe a three-mode avoided crossing, indicating strong coupling between the resonator, transmon, and NV ensemble.
result: Clear evidence of strong coupling is observed, with characteristic splitting in the transmission spectrum.
conclusion: This work establishes a solid-state platform for coherent interactions between disparate quantum systems, enabling future quantum networking and transduction applications.

title: Optimal Work Extraction From Finite-time Closed Quantum Dynamics
authors: Shoki Sugimoto, Takahiro Sagawa, And Ryusuke Hamazaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shoki Sugimoto, Takahiro Sagawa, and Ryusuke Hamazaki

Extracting useful work from quantum systems is a fundamental problem in quantum thermodynamics. In scenarios where rapid protocols are desired—whether due to practical constraints or deliberate design choices—a fundamental trade-off between power and efficiency is yet to be established. Here, we inv…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023321] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a fundamental trade-off between power and efficiency in finite-time quantum work extraction from closed systems, deriving optimal protocols and bounds.
motivation: Rapid work extraction protocols are practically important, but the trade-off between power and efficiency in quantum thermodynamics was not well understood.
method: The authors use optimal control theory and quantum thermodynamic principles to analyze work extraction from closed quantum systems under finite-time constraints.
result: They derive fundamental bounds on the maximum extractable work and efficiency as functions of protocol duration, revealing a power-efficiency trade-off.
conclusion: The results provide a theoretical framework for designing optimal finite-time quantum engines and highlight the role of quantum coherence in work extraction.

title: Thermodynamic Irreversibility In Optical Bistability
authors: G. Keijsers, R. M. de Boer, B. Verdonschot, K. J. H. Peters, And S. R. K. Rodriguez
abstract:
Author(s): G. Keijsers, R. M. de Boer, B. Verdonschot, K. J. H. Peters, and S. R. K. Rodriguez

We demonstrate thermodynamic irreversibility in the stochastic switching of a coherently driven bistable optical cavity. We present measurements of phase space probability currents evidencing the breaking of detailed balance associated with thermodynamic irreversibility. We also estimate the magnitu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253803] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of thermodynamic irreversibility in a bistable optical cavity via phase space probability currents and entropy production estimation.
motivation: To directly observe and quantify thermodynamic irreversibility in a driven optical system, linking stochastic switching to non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
method: Measurements of phase space probability currents in a coherently driven bistable optical cavity, with estimation of entropy production rate.
result: Clear evidence of broken detailed balance and finite entropy production, demonstrating irreversibility in the switching dynamics.
conclusion: Optical bistability provides a clean platform for studying non-equilibrium thermodynamics and irreversible processes at the mesoscopic scale.

title: Shake Before Use: Universal Enhancement Of Quantum Thermometry By Unitary Driving
authors: Emanuele Tumbiolo, Lorenzo Maccone, Chiara Macchiavello, Matteo G. A. Paris, And Giacomo Guarnieri
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuele Tumbiolo, Lorenzo Maccone, Chiara Macchiavello, Matteo G. A. Paris, and Giacomo Guarnieri

Quantum thermometry aims at determining temperature with ultimate precision in the quantum regime. Standard equilibrium approaches, limited by the quantum Fisher information given by static energy fluctuations, lose sensitivity outside a fixed temperature window. Nonequilibrium strategies have there…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250401] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Universal enhancement of quantum thermometry precision via unitary driving, overcoming equilibrium limitations.
motivation: Standard equilibrium quantum thermometry loses sensitivity outside a fixed temperature window; nonequilibrium strategies are needed to achieve high precision over a broader range.
method: The authors propose applying a unitary driving protocol to the probe system, analyzing the quantum Fisher information and deriving conditions for universal enhancement.
result: Unitary driving universally improves the precision of temperature estimation, with the enhancement quantified by the variance of the driving Hamiltonian.
conclusion: The protocol offers a practical, model-independent method to boost quantum thermometry performance, relevant for quantum technologies and thermodynamics.

title: Entanglement Entropy From Correlation Functions Of Scalar Fields In And Out Of Equilibrium
authors: Mrinal Kanti Sarkar, Saranyo Moitra, And Rajdeep Sensarma
abstract:
Author(s): Mrinal Kanti Sarkar, Saranyo Moitra, and Rajdeep Sensarma

We show that odd order Rényi entropies [MATH] of a system of interacting scalar fields can be calculated as the free energy of [MATH] replicas of the system with additional quadratic inter-replica couplings in the subsystem at the time of measurement of the entropy. These couplings replace b…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062463] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a method to compute odd-order Rényi entropies for interacting scalar fields using replica trick with quadratic inter-replica couplings, and applies it to equilibrium and non-equilibrium settings.
motivation: Entanglement entropy is a key measure in quantum information and many-body physics, but its calculation for interacting field theories, especially out of equilibrium, is challenging. The authors aim to provide a practical computational framework.
method: They show that odd-order Rényi entropies can be expressed as the free energy of replicated systems with additional quadratic couplings in the subsystem at the measurement time. This reduces the problem to computing Gaussian path integrals, which they evaluate analytically for free fields and perturbatively for interacting fields.
result: They obtain explicit expressions for Rényi entropies in equilibrium and for a quantum quench protocol, demonstrating how the entropy evolves and depends on interaction strength.
conclusion: The method provides a tractable way to compute entanglement measures in interacting quantum field theories, both in and out of equilibrium, and can be extended to other settings.

title: Heat, Work, And Fluctuations In A Driven Quantum Resonator
authors: Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, And Christian Flindt
abstract:
Author(s): Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, and Christian Flindt

A central building block of a heat engine is the working fluid, which mediates the conversion of heat into work. In nanoscale heat engines, the working fluid can be a quantum system whose behavior and dynamics are nonclassical. A particularly versatile realization is a quantum resonator, which allow…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064151] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies heat, work, and fluctuations in a driven quantum resonator, a model system for nanoscale heat engines.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamics of quantum systems is crucial for designing efficient nanoscale heat engines. The quantum resonator is a versatile working fluid whose nonclassical behavior can impact performance.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a driven quantum resonator coupled to thermal baths, using full counting statistics and fluctuation theorems to characterize heat and work distributions.
result: They derive exact expressions for the heat and work statistics, revealing non-Gaussian fluctuations and quantum signatures such as discreteness and coherence effects.
conclusion: The work provides a fundamental understanding of energy exchange in driven quantum systems, with implications for optimizing quantum heat engines and understanding thermodynamic bounds.

title: Universal Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation For Quantum $f$ Divergences
authors: Domingos S. P. Salazar
abstract:
Author(s): Domingos S. P. Salazar

We show that any Petz [MATH] divergence (where [MATH] is operator convex) between quantum states admits a universal [MATH]-mixture representation: the distinguishability of [MATH] from [MATH] is obtained as a positive superposition of quadratic contrasts [MATH], with non-negative weights [MATH] …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064150] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves a universal thermodynamic uncertainty relation for quantum f-divergences, linking distinguishability to thermodynamic cost.
motivation: To understand fundamental thermodynamic constraints on information processing in quantum systems, specifically how distinguishability of quantum states relates to dissipation.
method: The authors show that any Petz f-divergence can be expressed as a positive superposition of quadratic contrasts, leading to a universal bound on the rate of change of distinguishability in terms of thermodynamic quantities.
result: A universal thermodynamic uncertainty relation is derived for quantum f-divergences, generalizing previous results and providing a unified framework for thermodynamic bounds on information measures.
conclusion: The work establishes a deep connection between quantum information theory and thermodynamics, offering new insights into the thermodynamic cost of distinguishing quantum states.

title: Detecting Quantum Noise Of A Solid-state Spin Ensemble With Dispersive Measurement
authors: Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, and Aashish A. Clerk

We theoretically explore protocols for measuring the spin polarization of an ensemble of solid-state spins, with precision at or below the standard quantum limit. Such measurements in the solid state are challenging, as standard approaches based on optical fluorescence are often limited by poor read…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023331] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically explores dispersive measurement protocols for solid-state spin ensembles to detect spin polarization with precision at or below the standard quantum limit.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum memories and sensors, but measuring their polarization with high precision is challenging due to poor optical readout efficiency.
method: The authors analyze dispersive measurement schemes where the spin ensemble is coupled to a cavity or resonator, and the measurement is performed via phase shifts or transmission changes.
result: They show that with optimized parameters, the measurement can reach or surpass the standard quantum limit, enabling detection of quantum noise and spin squeezing.
conclusion: Dispersive measurement is a viable route for high-precision spin ensemble readout in solid-state platforms, with applications in quantum sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Stochastic Schrödinger Equations For Quantum Reverse Diffusion
authors: Einar Gabbassov
abstract:
Author(s): Einar Gabbassov

The ensemble-averaged dynamics of open quantum systems are typically irreversible. We show that this irreversibility need not hold at the level of individually monitored quantum trajectories. Our main results are analytical stochastic Schrödinger equations for quantum reverse diffusion, along with c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023329] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that irreversibility in open quantum systems can be avoided at the level of individual quantum trajectories, deriving stochastic Schrödinger equations for reverse diffusion.
motivation: Standard open quantum system dynamics are irreversible due to ensemble averaging, but the authors ask whether this irreversibility is fundamental or can be circumvented by monitoring individual trajectories.
method: The authors derive analytical stochastic Schrödinger equations that describe reverse diffusion of quantum trajectories, using tools from stochastic calculus and quantum measurement theory.
result: They obtain explicit equations for the time-reversed evolution of quantum trajectories, demonstrating that the reverse process is governed by a different stochastic equation than the forward process.
conclusion: The irreversibility of open quantum systems is not inherent at the trajectory level; reverse diffusion is possible, which has implications for quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Experimental Measurement And A Physical Interpretation Of Quantum Shadow Enumerators
authors: Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, And Jens Eisert
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, and Jens Eisert

This article shows that Rains’ quantum shadow enumerators, a powerful tool in quantum error correction, admit a direct physical interpretation in terms of outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements. This connection enables efficient learning protocols for these quantities and is demonstrated experimentally on a trapped-ion quantum device.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023318] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a physical interpretation of quantum shadow enumerators in terms of two-copy Bell measurements and demonstrates their efficient experimental measurement on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
motivation: Quantum shadow enumerators are powerful tools for analyzing quantum error-correcting codes, but they lacked a direct physical interpretation and efficient experimental measurement protocols.
method: The authors show that Rains' quantum shadow enumerators correspond to outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements, enabling efficient learning via randomized measurements. They implement this on a trapped-ion device.
result: They experimentally measure shadow enumerators for small error-correcting codes, validating the theoretical connection and demonstrating the practicality of the approach.
conclusion: This work bridges a gap between abstract quantum error correction theory and experimental implementation, providing a new tool for characterizing quantum codes.

title: Steady-state Entanglement Of Spin Qubits Mediated By Nonreciprocal And Chiral Magnons
authors: Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, And Silvia Viola Kusminskiy
abstract:
Author(s): Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, and Silvia Viola Kusminskiy

We propose a hybrid quantum system in which a magnet supporting nonreciprocal magnons, chiral magnons, or both mediates the dissipative and unidirectional coupling of spin qubits. By driving the qubits, the steady state of this qubit-qubit coupling scheme becomes the maximally entangled Bell state. …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023310] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid quantum system using nonreciprocal and chiral magnons in a magnet to mediate dissipative, unidirectional coupling of spin qubits, achieving steady-state Bell state entanglement.
motivation: To generate steady-state entanglement between spin qubits without active feedback or fine-tuning, leveraging the unique properties of magnons in magnetic systems.
method: The system consists of spin qubits coupled to a magnet that supports nonreciprocal or chiral magnons. By driving the qubits, the magnon-mediated interaction becomes dissipative and unidirectional, leading to a steady state that is a maximally entangled Bell state.
result: The steady state of the qubit-qubit coupling scheme is the maximally entangled Bell state, achieved through the engineered dissipative dynamics.
conclusion: This hybrid platform offers a robust method for generating entanglement in quantum networks, combining spin qubits with magnonic systems for scalable quantum information processing.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity; tin-vacancy centers in diamond offer promising optical properties but achieving strong coupling has been challenging.
method: Fabricated nanophotonic photonic crystal cavities in diamond with embedded tin-vacancy centers and characterized the cavity-spin coupling via resonant reflection and lifetime measurements.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity >1, indicating strong coupling regime, with high Purcell factor and low spectral diffusion.
conclusion: This platform enables deterministic entanglement generation and is a key building block for future quantum repeaters and distributed quantum computing.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To provide a clear and general criterion for nonclassicality in quantum processes, beyond standard signatures like entanglement or Bell nonlocality.
method: Develops a theoretical framework based on the process matrix formalism and defines nonclassicality via the inability to simulate a process with classical resources.
result: The rule recovers many known quantum signatures and identifies new nonclassical features in processes previously considered classical, such as certain types of quantum channels.
conclusion: The work refines the boundary between classical and quantum, with implications for understanding quantum resources and developing quantum technologies.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement is a key resource for quantum sensing and many-body physics, but it is fragile and difficult to stabilize. The authors aim to turn cavity noise, typically detrimental, into a tool for generating and controlling multipartite entanglement.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a squeezed reservoir or feedback, leading to steady-state entanglement that can be reconfigured by tuning parameters.
result: They show that the system can produce various entangled states, including spin-squeezed states and topological states, with high fidelity and robustness against imperfections. The entanglement is dissipatively stabilized, eliminating the need for precise initial state preparation.
conclusion: The approach provides a scalable and flexible platform for generating multipartite entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, with immediate applications in quantum sensing and simulation of many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and improve performance.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect a qubit against photon loss, operating at the breakeven point where the corrected lifetime surpasses the uncorrected physical limit.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended beyond the physical limit, demonstrating passive error correction at breakeven for the first time.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can outperform active schemes in certain regimes, offering a new path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers that midcircuit measurements can exponentially extend the lifetime of quantum information in monitored quantum dynamics, revealing scaling laws for information survival.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect quantum information is crucial for quantum computing and communication, especially for error mitigation and memory protection.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, deriving scaling laws for the quantum information lifetime using statistical mechanics mappings and numerical simulations.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size when measurements are frequent enough, and identify a phase transition between information-preserving and information-erasing regimes.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be harnessed to protect quantum information for exponentially long times, offering a practical strategy for near-term quantum devices.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental and numerical results on suppressing measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubits using a nonlinear cosφ coupling, aiming to improve readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors design a cosφ coupling element and perform experiments and numerical simulations to analyze the dynamics and suppression of state transitions during readout.
result: The nonlinear coupling significantly reduces measurement-induced transitions, leading to higher readout fidelity.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling approach offers a practical path to improve transmon readout, benefiting quantum error correction and fault-tolerant computing.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with sublinear experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin emitters are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited control. A scalable method to generate large cluster states is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework using global driving fields and optical heralding to entangle inhomogeneous spin ensembles, leveraging spin-photon interfaces and cavity coupling.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity entanglement generation and cluster state preparation with sublinear overhead, scaling to 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to programmable quantum matter using existing solid-state platforms, advancing hybrid quantum systems for networking and computation.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random measurements in a monitored quantum circuit can enhance the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes, linking measurement-induced phases to code performance.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, especially in the context of measurement-based protocols and monitored dynamics.
method: The authors analyze stabilizer codes under random projective measurements, using statistical mechanics mappings and percolation theory to characterize decoding transitions.
result: They find that random measurements can improve decoding thresholds and that the measurement-induced phase transition correlates with code performance, providing new insights into stability under partial measurement.
conclusion: Randomly monitored quantum codes offer a new perspective on error correction, suggesting that measurement can be a resource rather than a hindrance, with implications for fault-tolerant architectures.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chip implementing self-testing quantum random number generation, a core device-independent protocol.
motivation: To miniaturize and scale quantum security devices by integrating self-testing QRNG on a photonic chip, addressing practical deployment challenges.
method: Designs and fabricates a silicon photonic chipset that performs a self-testing quantum random number expansion protocol, leveraging device-independent randomness certification.
result: Achieves high-speed random number generation with provable security based on Bell inequality violation, all on a compact integrated platform.
conclusion: The work paves the way for production-scale quantum security devices by combining self-testing protocols with integrated photonics.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric tree-codes for quantum repeaters, significantly reducing resource requirements while maintaining loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing schemes require many resources. The authors aim to design more efficient tree-codes that are practical for near-term implementation.
method: They propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for quantum tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource overhead.
result: The optimized tree-codes achieve comparable or better loss tolerance with substantially fewer physical qubits and operations, improving repeater performance.
conclusion: The hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes offer a resource-efficient path toward practical quantum repeaters, advancing the feasibility of quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence and high-fidelity single-shot readout are demonstrated, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: To identify and characterize a solid-state spin defect with long coherence and high readout fidelity for quantum information processing.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of deep-level defects in ZnO, focusing on electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence, and optical readout.
result: A deep defect in ZnO exhibits unusually small electron-phonon coupling, 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are viable new platforms for scalable quantum technologies, offering competitive spin properties.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Existing security proofs often assume ideal devices or worst-case noise, but real devices have known imperfections that can be characterized; incorporating this knowledge can improve key rates and enable certification.
method: The authors develop a modular framework that integrates device characterization data (e.g., loss, detector efficiency) into entropy accumulation theorem-based security proofs, using a 'characterization map' to bound the adversary's information.
result: The method yields tighter finite-key security bounds that account for realistic device parameters, and provides a clear path for standardizing QKD security certification.
conclusion: Device characterization can be rigorously incorporated into composable security proofs, bridging theory and practice for QKD certification.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby flagging erasure events.
result: The erasure conversion scheme significantly boosts effective coherence times by turning dominant relaxation errors into detectable erasures.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to improved error correction by converting relaxation errors into erasures, enhancing quantum computing performance.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Cavity-mode multiplexing enables parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in a neutral-atom array, scaling up quantum computing and networking.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays with cavity-enhanced operations are limited by serial addressing; multiplexing allows parallel processing for scalability.
method: The paper proposes and analyzes a scheme where multiple cavity modes are used to simultaneously address different atoms or groups in an array, leveraging spatial mode separation.
result: The scheme shows that cavity-mode multiplexing can significantly increase the rate of entangling operations and reduce overhead, making large-scale neutral-atom quantum processors feasible.
conclusion: Mode multiplexing is a promising approach to scale cavity-enhanced operations in neutral-atom arrays, advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum computing and networking.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous >99.9% fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device through careful tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: High-fidelity gates and readout are essential for scalable quantum computing, but achieving all simultaneously in a single device remains challenging.
method: The authors optimize qubit-coupler interactions and develop a novel calibration protocol to minimize crosstalk and errors across all operations.
result: They achieve >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in the same superconducting device.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that simultaneous high-fidelity operations are feasible, paving the way for larger-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random quantum codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics and random matrix theory, studying the spectral properties of the code's density matrix and the decoding transition under local noise.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases, governed by the spectral gap of the code's density matrix, and provide a simple analytical description of the transition.
conclusion: The work provides fundamental insights into the error-correcting capabilities of random quantum codes and establishes a clear phase transition mechanism, which may inform the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, as classical gravity cannot generate entanglement between quantum probes; information-theoretic methods provide a framework to design experiments that can distinguish between classical and quantum theories of gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical proposals for tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two massive quantum probes, analyzing the information-theoretic constraints and experimental feasibility.
result: Several feasible GIE experiments are identified that could test the quantum nature of gravity, with detailed analysis of their requirements and potential outcomes.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a concrete path to experimentally test the quantumness of gravity, and proposed GIE experiments are within reach of current technology.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscale to macroscopic deterministic thermodynamics using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework that connects mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics with macroscopic thermodynamic laws, addressing systems far from equilibrium.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, avoiding traditional Langevin approaches.
result: Constructs a thermodynamically consistent framework for rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical networks, electronic circuits, and Potts models.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, challenging conventional Langevin-based methods.

title: Clifford Hierarchy Stabilizer Codes: Transversal Non-Clifford Gates And Magic States
authors: Ryohei Kobayashi, Guanyu Zhu, And Po-Shen Hsin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryohei Kobayashi, Guanyu Zhu, and Po-Shen Hsin

A fundamental problem in fault-tolerant quantum computation is the tradeoff between universality and dimensionality, exemplified by the Bravyi-König bound for [MATH]-dimensional topological stabilizer codes. In this Letter, we extend topological Pauli stabilizer codes to a broad class of [MATH]-dimensiona…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250802] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends topological stabilizer codes to higher dimensions to achieve transversal non-Clifford gates and magic state distillation, overcoming the Bravyi-König bound.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires universal gate sets, but transversal gates are limited by the Bravyi-König bound for 2D topological codes. The authors aim to circumvent this by considering higher-dimensional codes.
method: The paper introduces Clifford hierarchy stabilizer codes in arbitrary dimensions, constructing codes that support transversal non-Clifford gates (e.g., T gate) and analyzing their properties using algebraic topology and cohomology.
result: They demonstrate that certain higher-dimensional codes allow transversal implementation of gates from the third level of the Clifford hierarchy, enabling universal computation via magic state distillation without sacrificing fault tolerance.
conclusion: Higher-dimensional topological stabilizer codes provide a viable path to universal fault-tolerant quantum computation with transversal gates, offering a new direction beyond 2D limitations.

title: Many-Body Perturbation Theory For Driven Dissipative Quasiparticle Flows And Fluctuations
authors: Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, And Vojtech Vlcek
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, and Vojtech Vlcek

We present a unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing. Using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism, we introduce a diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines representing quasiparticle flows and fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256403] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism.
motivation: To develop a theoretical framework that can handle driven dissipative quantum systems with strong correlations, which are common in quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.
method: The authors combine Keldysh Green's functions with Lindblad master equations to construct a diagrammatic perturbation theory where dissipative interactions are represented as quasiparticle flows and fluctuations.
result: The formalism yields a systematic expansion for observables and correlation functions, capturing both coherent and dissipative dynamics in a unified manner.
conclusion: This work provides a powerful tool for analyzing non-equilibrium quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: When Hidden Conservation Laws Prevent Directed Currents In Stochastic Systems
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The emergence of nonequilibrium currents has attracted a lot of attention. The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of any form of parity and time-reversal symmetries as the necessary conditions for the emergence of such currents. Here we study active and passive systems with asymmetric spat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 257102] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper revisits the ratchet principle for stochastic systems, showing that hidden conservation laws can prevent directed currents even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are broken.
motivation: To understand necessary conditions for directed transport in nonequilibrium systems, specifically why some asymmetric systems fail to produce net currents.
method: The authors analyze active and passive stochastic systems with asymmetric spatial potentials, identifying hidden conservation laws that suppress currents despite broken symmetries.
result: They demonstrate that hidden conservation laws can prevent directed currents, refining the ratchet principle.
conclusion: The ratchet principle is incomplete; hidden conservation laws must be considered to predict directed transport in stochastic systems.

title: Probing Quantum States Over Spacetime Through Interferometry
authors: Seok Hyung Lie And Hyukjoon Kwon
abstract:
Author(s): Seok Hyung Lie and Hyukjoon Kwon

Establishing a notion of the quantum state that applies consistently across space and time could be a crucial step toward formulating a relativistic quantum theory. We give an operational meaning to multipartite quantum states over arbitrary regions in spacetime through a causally agnostic measureme…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250201] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a causally agnostic measurement scheme to operationally define multipartite quantum states over arbitrary spacetime regions using interferometry.
motivation: To establish a consistent notion of quantum states across space and time, which is crucial for formulating a relativistic quantum theory.
method: The authors develop a causally agnostic measurement framework that allows probing quantum states in spacetime without assuming a fixed causal structure, using interferometric setups.
result: They show that multipartite quantum states can be operationally defined and verified over arbitrary spacetime regions, providing a new perspective on quantum correlations in spacetime.
conclusion: This work offers a practical approach to characterizing quantum states in relativistic settings, potentially impacting quantum information and foundational studies.

title: Thermodynamics Of Black Holes, Far From Equilibrium
authors: Abhay Ashtekar, Daniel E. Paraizo, And Jonathan Shu
abstract:
Author(s): Abhay Ashtekar, Daniel E. Paraizo, and Jonathan Shu

The first law of black hole mechanics has been extended to dynamical horizons so that the law applies to black holes arbitrarily far from equilibrium, a fundamental result that formally shows the thermodynamic description of black holes extends beyond the typical stationary solutions.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251405] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Extends the first law of black hole mechanics to dynamical horizons, showing thermodynamic behavior holds far from equilibrium.
motivation: To understand whether black holes obey thermodynamic laws beyond stationary equilibrium, which is crucial for quantum gravity and information thermodynamics.
method: Uses dynamical horizon formalism and geometric analysis to derive a first law for non-stationary black holes.
result: Establishes a first law for dynamical horizons, linking changes in horizon area to energy and angular momentum fluxes.
conclusion: Black hole thermodynamics applies even far from equilibrium, reinforcing the deep connection between gravity and thermodynamics.

title: Enhancing Nonreciprocity Through Squeezing-Induced Symmetry Breaking
authors: B.-B. Liu, D.-Y. Wang, J. Tang, G. Chen, H. Jing, Shi-Lei Su, And F. Nori
abstract:
Author(s): B.-B. Liu, D.-Y. Wang, J. Tang, G. Chen, H. Jing, Shi-Lei Su, and F. Nori

Reservoir engineering enables unidirectional energy and signal flow. We establish squeezing-induced symmetry breaking between two cavities as a guiding principle for exponentially amplifying reservoir-mediated nonreciprocity. Rather than a simple scaling of the coupling, this mechanism strategically…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253602] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Squeezing-induced symmetry breaking between two cavities exponentially amplifies reservoir-mediated nonreciprocity.
motivation: To achieve strong nonreciprocal signal flow in quantum systems, which is crucial for quantum networks and information processing.
method: The authors engineer a squeezed reservoir that couples to two cavities, breaking the symmetry between them and enabling unidirectional energy transfer.
result: The nonreciprocity is exponentially amplified compared to simple coupling scaling, demonstrating a new guiding principle for reservoir engineering.
conclusion: Squeezing-induced symmetry breaking provides a powerful mechanism for enhancing nonreciprocity, with potential applications in quantum transducers and isolators.

title: Machine-Learned Tuning To Protected States By Probing Noise Resilience
authors: Rodrigo A. Dourado, Nicolás Martínez-Valero, Jacob Benestad, Martin Leijnse, Jeroen Danon, And Rubén Seoane Souto
abstract:
Author(s): Rodrigo A. Dourado, Nicolás Martínez-Valero, Jacob Benestad, Martin Leijnse, Jeroen Danon, and Rubén Seoane Souto

Protected states are promising for quantum technologies due to their intrinsic resilience against noise. However, such states often emerge at discrete points or small regions in parameter space and are, thus, difficult to find in experiments. In this Letter, we present a machine-learning method for …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256604] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A machine-learning method to tune quantum devices into protected states by probing noise resilience.
motivation: Protected states are robust against noise but hard to locate in parameter space; manual tuning is inefficient.
method: Uses a machine-learning algorithm that iteratively probes noise resilience to navigate parameter space and identify protected regions.
result: Demonstrates successful tuning to protected states in a simulated or experimental quantum system, showing improved noise resilience.
conclusion: Machine learning can efficiently discover protected states, aiding in the practical deployment of noise-resilient quantum technologies.

title: Squeezing-Enhanced Sensing At An Exceptional Point
authors: Changqing Wang, Deyuan Hu, Silvia Zorzetti, Anna Grassellino, Alexander Romanenko, And Zheshen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Changqing Wang, Deyuan Hu, Silvia Zorzetti, Anna Grassellino, Alexander Romanenko, and Zheshen Zhang

Pushing the boundaries of measurement precision is central for sensing and metrology, pursued by nonclassical resources such as squeezing, as well as non-Hermitian degeneracies with distinct spectral response. Their convergence, however, remains challenging. We find extraordinary enhancement of sens…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250801] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that combining squeezing with exceptional points in a non-Hermitian system yields extraordinary enhancement of sensing precision beyond conventional limits.
motivation: Squeezing and exceptional points are two powerful but separate approaches to enhance measurement precision; their combination has been challenging but promises significant improvements for quantum sensing.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally realize a non-Hermitian system where squeezing is introduced at an exceptional point, analyzing the resulting sensitivity enhancement using quantum noise analysis.
result: They find that the synergy between squeezing and exceptional points leads to a sensitivity scaling that surpasses both standard quantum limit and the limit from exceptional points alone.
conclusion: This work opens a new avenue for ultra-precise sensing by merging nonclassical resources with non-Hermitian degeneracies, with potential applications in quantum metrology and fundamental physics.

title: Noncommutative Index Of Measurement-only Entanglement Phase Transitions
authors: Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, And Zhisong Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, and Zhisong Xiao

Measurement-only models offer an ideal platform for exploring entanglement dynamics in the absence of unitary evolution. Despite extensive numerical evidence for entanglement phase transitions in measurement-only dynamics, the underlying mechanism attributed to noncommutativity among multisite proje…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062223] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies noncommutativity as the mechanism driving entanglement phase transitions in measurement-only quantum circuits.
motivation: Measurement-only models exhibit entanglement phase transitions, but the underlying mechanism was unclear; this work aims to explain it via noncommutativity of multisite projectors.
method: The authors introduce a noncommutative index to characterize measurement-only dynamics and analyze its role in entanglement transitions using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They show that the noncommutative index determines the universality class of the entanglement phase transition, providing a unified framework for understanding these transitions.
conclusion: Noncommutativity is the key driver of measurement-only entanglement phase transitions, offering a new perspective on entanglement dynamics in quantum circuits.

title: Dynamical Irreversibility And Local Decoherence In Quantum Many-body Chaos
authors: Jose Alfredo de Leon, Miguel Gonzalez, And Carlos Diaz-Mejia
abstract:
Author(s): Jose Alfredo de Leon, Miguel Gonzalez, and Carlos Diaz-Mejia

Typical dynamical quantum chaos probes are initial-state dependent (e.g., local observables or purities) and thus may fail to capture typical decoherent behavior one expects of a subsystem. Quantum channels fully capture the reduced dynamics of a subsystem. Here, we investigate the purity of the Cho…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062224] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical irreversibility and local decoherence in quantum many-body systems using the purity of the Choi state of the reduced channel as a probe of chaos.
motivation: Typical quantum chaos probes are initial-state dependent and may not capture typical decoherent behavior; the authors aim to characterize chaos via the reduced dynamics of a subsystem.
method: They investigate the purity of the Choi state of the quantum channel describing the reduced dynamics, and relate it to the out-of-time-ordered correlator (OTOC) and operator entanglement.
result: The purity of the Choi state is shown to be a reliable probe of quantum chaos, capturing the onset of irreversibility and decoherence, and it connects to the growth of operator entanglement.
conclusion: The Choi state purity provides a universal, initial-state-independent measure of chaos and decoherence in many-body systems, linking information-theoretic and thermodynamic concepts.

title: Satellite-based Quantum Steering With Continuous Variables
authors: Qianqian Liu, Shu-Min Wu, Cuihong Wen, And Jieci Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Qianqian Liu, Shu-Min Wu, Cuihong Wen, and Jieci Wang

The Gaussian quantum steering in free space is a key resource for satellite-based quantum communication. In this work, we model the free space transmission of Gaussian states as a fading and noisy quantum channel, incorporating key loss mechanisms including diffraction, atmospheric attenuation, turb…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062462] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper models free-space transmission of Gaussian states for satellite-based quantum steering, analyzing the effects of diffraction, atmospheric attenuation, and turbulence.
motivation: Satellite-based quantum communication requires understanding how realistic channels affect quantum steering, a key resource for quantum networks.
method: The authors model the free-space channel as a fading and noisy Gaussian channel, incorporating loss mechanisms such as diffraction, atmospheric attenuation, and turbulence.
result: They quantify the degradation of Gaussian quantum steering under realistic satellite-to-ground channel conditions.
conclusion: The results provide insights into the feasibility of satellite-based quantum steering with continuous variables, informing the design of future quantum network architectures.

title: Spin Coherence Scale: Operator-ordering Sensitivity Beyond The Heisenberg-Weyl Group
authors: Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andre J. Rodrigues, Y. Batuhan Yilmaz, Aephraim M. Steinberg, And Anaelle Hertz
abstract:
Author(s): Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andre J. Rodrigues, Y. Batuhan Yilmaz, Aephraim M. Steinberg, and Anaelle Hertz

We introduce the spin coherence scale as a measure of quantum coherence for spin systems, generalizing the quadrature coherence scale (QCS) previously defined for quadrature observables. This SU(2)-invariant measure quantifies the off-diagonal coherences of a quantum state in angular momentum bases,…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062457] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a spin coherence scale as an SU(2)-invariant measure of quantum coherence for spin systems, generalizing the quadrature coherence scale.
motivation: Existing coherence measures are often basis-dependent or not tailored to spin systems; a scale that captures operator-ordering sensitivity beyond the Heisenberg-Weyl group is needed.
method: Defines the spin coherence scale using angular momentum operators and SU(2) invariance, and analyzes its properties for various spin states.
result: The measure quantifies off-diagonal coherences in angular momentum bases and exhibits operator-ordering sensitivity, providing a new tool for coherence characterization.
conclusion: The spin coherence scale offers a physically meaningful, invariant measure of coherence for spin systems, with potential applications in quantum information and metrology.

title: Scalable Quantum Resources With Short-range Interacting Spin-1/2 Chains
authors: Marcin Płodzień And Jan Chwedeńczuk
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień and Jan Chwedeńczuk

The dynamical generation of quantum resources, such as many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, or spin squeezing, can be achieved via one-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics, which require all-to-all couplings. However, current digital and analog quantum simulation platforms natively provide short-range…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062220] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains can generate scalable quantum resources like entanglement and Bell correlations via one-axis twisting dynamics, overcoming the need for all-to-all couplings.
motivation: One-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics generate useful quantum resources but require all-to-all couplings, which are not native to most quantum simulation platforms. The authors aim to achieve similar resource generation using short-range interactions.
method: The authors analyze spin-1/2 chains with short-range interactions and show that OAT-like dynamics emerge under certain conditions, enabling the generation of many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, and spin squeezing. They use analytical and numerical methods to characterize the resource scaling.
result: They demonstrate that scalable quantum resources can be generated in short-range interacting chains, with entanglement and Bell correlations growing with system size, and provide conditions for optimal resource generation.
conclusion: Short-range interacting spin chains are a viable platform for generating scalable quantum resources, offering a practical alternative to all-to-all coupling schemes for quantum information processing.

title: Gleason's Theorem For A Qubit As Part Of A Composite System
authors: Vincenzo Fiorentino And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Author(s): Vincenzo Fiorentino and Stefan Weigert

We extend Gleason's theorem to the two-dimensional Hilbert space of a qubit by invoking the standard axiom that describes composite quantum systems. The tensor-product structure allows us to derive density matrices and Born's rule for [MATH] from a simple requirement: the probabilities assigned to me…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062221] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Extends Gleason's theorem to qubits by using the tensor-product structure of composite systems to derive density matrices and Born's rule.
motivation: Gleason's theorem does not apply to two-dimensional Hilbert spaces; the authors aim to fill this gap by invoking the composite system axiom.
method: They assume that probabilities assigned to measurement outcomes on a qubit are consistent with the tensor-product structure when the qubit is part of a larger system, and derive the standard quantum formalism.
result: They show that the only consistent probability assignments are given by density matrices and Born's rule, thus proving a version of Gleason's theorem for qubits.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational justification for the quantum formalism in the simplest non-trivial case, reinforcing the role of composite systems in quantum theory.

title: Accelerated Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Quantum Memory Via Shortcuts To Adiabaticity
authors: Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, And X. Q. Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, and X. Q. Shao

Electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) enables coherent light-matter storage, forming the basis of photonic quantum memories that are essential for scalable quantum networks and distributed quantum computing. However, accelerating the storage process violates the adiabatic condition, resulti…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062453] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using shortcuts to adiabaticity to accelerate Rydberg EIT quantum memory, improving storage speed while maintaining high efficiency.
motivation: EIT-based quantum memories are crucial for quantum networks but are limited by slow adiabatic storage processes. Accelerating storage without sacrificing fidelity is a key challenge.
method: The authors apply counter-diabatic driving (shortcuts to adiabaticity) to the Rydberg EIT system, designing control pulses that suppress non-adiabatic errors and enable faster storage.
result: Numerical simulations show that the accelerated protocol achieves near-unity storage efficiency and fidelity with significantly shorter storage times compared to conventional adiabatic EIT.
conclusion: Shortcuts to adiabaticity offer a practical route to faster quantum memories, which could enhance the performance of quantum repeaters and network nodes.

title: Observing Fundamental Triple Uncertainty Relations
authors: Yan Wang, Jie Zhou, Xing-Yan Fan, Ze-Yan Hao, Jia-Kun Li, Zheng-Hao Liu, Ya Xiao, Kai Sun, Jin-Shi Xu, Jing-Ling Chen, Chuan-Feng Li, And Guang-Can Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Wang, Jie Zhou, Xing-Yan Fan, Ze-Yan Hao, Jia-Kun Li, Zheng-Hao Liu, Ya Xiao, Kai Sun, Jin-Shi Xu, Jing-Ling Chen, Chuan-Feng Li, and Guang-Can Guo

The uncertainty principle, arising from the incompatibility of noncommuting observables, constitutes one of the cornerstones of quantum mechanics. While uncertainty relations involving pairs of observables have been extensively investigated, experimentally accessible tight uncertainty relations for …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062447] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of tight triple uncertainty relations for three incompatible observables using photonic systems.
motivation: To test fundamental quantum uncertainty relations beyond pairwise ones, which are less explored experimentally.
method: Implemented a photonic experiment with polarization and path qubits to measure triple uncertainty relations based on sum of variances and entropic measures.
result: Observed tight triple uncertainty relations that are stronger than those derived from pairwise relations, confirming theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work provides experimental evidence for fundamental triple uncertainty relations, advancing understanding of quantum incompatibility.

title: Equilibrium Thermometry In The Multilevel Quantum Rabi Model
authors: Tabitha Doicin, Luis A. Correa, Jonas Glatthard, Andrew D. Armour, And Gerardo Adesso
abstract:
Author(s): Tabitha Doicin, Luis A. Correa, Jonas Glatthard, Andrew D. Armour, and Gerardo Adesso

The temperature sensitivity of a probe in equilibrium can be gauged by its thermal quantum Fisher information (QFI). It is known that probes exhibiting degeneracy in their energy-level structure can achieve larger sensitivities, while probes with a more uniform spectrum may remain sensitive over a b…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062449] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the temperature sensitivity of a quantum probe in equilibrium using the quantum Rabi model, finding that degeneracy in the energy spectrum enhances sensitivity.
motivation: Quantum thermometry at the nanoscale is important for applications in quantum technologies, and understanding how probe structure affects sensitivity is key.
method: The authors compute the thermal quantum Fisher information for the multilevel quantum Rabi model, analyzing the role of energy-level degeneracy and spectrum uniformity.
result: Probes with degenerate energy levels achieve larger temperature sensitivities, while those with uniform spectra remain sensitive over a broader temperature range.
conclusion: The quantum Rabi model provides a tunable platform for equilibrium thermometry, with degeneracy offering a trade-off between peak sensitivity and range.

title: Coupling-energy Driven Pumping Through Quantum Dots: Role Of Coherences
authors: Lukas Litzba, Gernot Schaller, Jürgen König, And Nikodem Szpak
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas Litzba, Gernot Schaller, Jürgen König, and Nikodem Szpak

We study the impact of off-resonant tunneling and coherences on the electron pumping through quantum dots. Thereby, we focus on two electron-pump setups where lowest-order tunneling processes are suppressed and the pump is exclusively driven by modulations of the coupling energy. The first setup is …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235152] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies electron pumping through quantum dots driven solely by coupling energy modulations, focusing on the role of off-resonant tunneling and coherences.
motivation: To understand how coherences and higher-order tunneling processes affect pumping in quantum dot systems where lowest-order processes are suppressed.
method: The authors analyze two specific pump setups using theoretical models that incorporate off-resonant tunneling and quantum coherences, likely via master equation or scattering matrix approaches.
result: They find that coherences and off-resonant tunneling significantly influence the pumping current and its direction, enabling pumping even when lowest-order processes are forbidden.
conclusion: Coupling-energy driven pumping is a viable mechanism for quantum dot systems, and coherences play a crucial role that must be accounted for in device design.

title: Entanglement Rényi Negativity Across The Finite-temperature Transition In The $o(3)$ Universality Class
authors: Dong-Xu Liu, Yi-Ming Ding, Zhe Wang, And Zheng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Dong-Xu Liu, Yi-Ming Ding, Zhe Wang, and Zheng Yan

The fate of quantum entanglement at finite-temperature phase transitions remains an open question, particularly for continuous symmetry breaking where zero-temperature Goldstone modes generate long-range correlations. Using large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we investigate the third Rényi …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245145] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the third Rényi negativity across a finite-temperature phase transition in the O(3) universality class using quantum Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: The fate of quantum entanglement at finite-temperature phase transitions, especially with continuous symmetry breaking, is not well understood.
method: Large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations are used to compute the third Rényi negativity across the transition.
result: The third Rényi negativity shows a peak at the transition temperature and obeys scaling laws consistent with the O(3) universality class.
conclusion: Entanglement measures like Rényi negativity can detect finite-temperature phase transitions and provide insight into the interplay of thermal and quantum fluctuations.

title: Dissipation And Fluctuations Of Cmos Ring Oscillators Close To Criticality
authors: Ashwin Gopal, Massimiliano Esposito, And Jan Meibohm
abstract:
Author(s): Ashwin Gopal, Massimiliano Esposito, and Jan Meibohm

We analyze a thermodynamically consistent model of Complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor-based ring oscillators near the onset of coherent voltage oscillations. For driving voltages close to the critical value, we derive the normal form of the Hopf bifurcation that underlies the oscillation transi…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245308] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes dissipation and fluctuations in CMOS ring oscillators near a Hopf bifurcation, deriving thermodynamic constraints on coherent oscillations.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost and fluctuations of CMOS oscillators near criticality is important for designing energy-efficient computing devices.
method: The authors develop a thermodynamically consistent model of CMOS ring oscillators and derive the normal form of the Hopf bifurcation underlying the oscillation transition.
result: They obtain expressions for dissipation and fluctuations near the critical driving voltage, linking the onset of oscillations to thermodynamic quantities.
conclusion: The work provides a thermodynamic perspective on CMOS oscillator dynamics, highlighting trade-offs between coherence, dissipation, and fluctuations near criticality.

title: Accuracy Comes At A Cost: Optimal Localization Against A Flow
authors: Till Welker And Patrick Pietzonka
abstract:
Author(s): Till Welker and Patrick Pietzonka

How can a small swimmer stay close to a target, while struggling against a flow and also being hit by the water molecules around it? The authors investigate this question in a simple setup, and find that the optimal navigation strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming with a trade-off between cost and accuracy.


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064142] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Optimal navigation strategy for a small swimmer in a flow trades off accuracy and cost, revealing thermodynamic constraints on information processing.
motivation: Understand how a microscopic swimmer can localize near a target despite flow and thermal noise, and quantify the fundamental trade-off between accuracy and energy cost.
method: The authors model a swimmer with active control and passive drift, using stochastic thermodynamics to derive optimal strategies that minimize a cost function combining accuracy and dissipation.
result: The optimal strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming, with a clear trade-off: higher accuracy requires more energy dissipation, and the optimal cost scales with the desired precision.
conclusion: The work establishes a thermodynamic bound on localization accuracy in a flow, linking information-theoretic limits to physical constraints, relevant for active matter and biological navigation.

title: Protocol For Purifying Noisy Preparation And Measurements Of Qubits
authors: Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Author(s): Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, and Joonwoo Bae

Noise affecting qubit preparation and measurements accounts for a significant fraction of errors in quantum information processing. This is especially critical in tasks like variational quantum algorithms, quantum error correction, and entanglement distribution through repeaters. In this work, we pr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023347] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A protocol to purify noisy qubit preparation and measurements using only trusted state preparation and trusted measurements, with security against untrusted devices.
motivation: Noise in qubit preparation and measurements is a major error source in quantum information processing, affecting tasks like variational algorithms, error correction, and entanglement distribution.
method: The protocol uses a trusted source and trusted measurement device to certify and purify noisy preparation and measurement devices via a semi-device-independent approach, leveraging linear programming and convex optimization.
result: The protocol can purify arbitrary noisy qubit states and measurements to near-perfect ones, with explicit bounds on the required number of rounds and noise tolerance.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method to improve qubit quality without full device independence, relevant for near-term quantum technologies.

title: Full Counting Statistics After Quantum Quenches As Hydrodynamic Fluctuations
authors: Dávid X. Horváth, Benjamin Doyon, And Paola Ruggiero
abstract:
Author(s): Dávid X. Horváth, Benjamin Doyon, and Paola Ruggiero

The statistics of fluctuations on large regions of space encodes universal properties of many-body systems. At equilibrium, it is described by thermodynamics. However, away from equilibrium such as after quantum quenches, the fundamental principles are more nebulous. In particular, although exact re…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023350] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a hydrodynamic theory for the full counting statistics of particle transport after quantum quenches, connecting non-equilibrium fluctuations to thermodynamic principles.
motivation: Understanding fluctuations in non-equilibrium many-body systems is fundamental, but a general framework beyond equilibrium thermodynamics is lacking. The authors aim to fill this gap by deriving exact results for the statistics of transferred charge after a quantum quench.
method: Using generalized hydrodynamics (GHD) and large-deviation theory, they compute the full counting statistics of particle transport in integrable models, treating the quench as a step initial state and analyzing the hydrodynamic fluctuations.
