result: They obtain exact expressions for the cumulant generating function and show that the statistics follow a universal form governed by the ballistic propagation of quasiparticles, with fluctuations scaling linearly in time.
conclusion: The work establishes a hydrodynamic framework for non-equilibrium fluctuations, revealing that the full counting statistics after a quench can be understood as a consequence of ballistic transport and initial state correlations, with potential extensions to other observables and models.

title: Surface Code Stabilizer Measurements For Rydberg Atoms
authors: Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, And Guido Pupillo
abstract:
Author(s): Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, and Guido Pupillo

Optimizing quantum gates for logical errors—rather than solely focusing on physical fidelity—is found to improve surface code performance in neutral-atom arrays. Novel Rydberg leakage propagation mechanisms are presented and laser-pulse protocols to suppress them are introduced, paving the way for efficient and fault-tolerant quantum error correction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022059] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Optimizing Rydberg atom gates for logical errors improves surface code performance and introduces protocols to suppress leakage.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but gate errors and leakage limit fault-tolerant error correction.
method: The authors analyze surface code stabilizer measurements in Rydberg atom arrays, optimizing gates for logical error rates and proposing laser-pulse protocols to mitigate leakage propagation.
result: They demonstrate improved surface code performance by focusing on logical errors rather than physical fidelity, and identify novel leakage mechanisms specific to Rydberg systems.
conclusion: The work provides practical strategies for fault-tolerant quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms, advancing their viability for large-scale quantum computing.

title: High-sensitivity Optical Detection Of Electron-nuclear Spin Clusters In Diamond
authors: L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, And G. Hétet
abstract:
Author(s): L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, and G. Hétet

We perform sensitive nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) with spin ensembles that are polarized by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond at room temperature. Using stabilized lasers, a balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field, we resolve sharp NMR features arising from multiple spin c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023337] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-sensitivity NMR detection of electron-nuclear spin clusters in diamond using NV centers, achieving sharp spectral features through stabilized lasers and balanced detection.
motivation: To improve sensitivity and spectral resolution in NMR detection of spin ensembles, leveraging NV centers for polarization and readout.
method: NV centers in diamond are used to polarize nuclear spins, and optical detection with stabilized lasers and balanced detection is employed to read out NMR signals under a highly uniform magnetic field.
result: Sharp NMR features from multiple spin clusters are resolved, demonstrating high sensitivity and spectral resolution.
conclusion: The technique enables sensitive detection of nuclear spin clusters, with potential applications in quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Parastatistics And A Secret Communication Challenge
authors: Zhiyuan Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Wang

A secret-communication challenge is proposed that demonstrates a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles in topological phases of matter. The work shows how exchanging emergent paraparticles can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance that is achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022056] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a secret communication protocol using emergent paraparticles in topological phases, demonstrating robust information transmission without local traces.
motivation: To demonstrate a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles and their potential for secure communication.
method: Theoretical analysis of exchanging emergent paraparticles in topological phases of matter, showing how information can be encoded and transmitted.
result: The protocol enables robust secret communication that leaves no locally detectable traces, achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.
conclusion: Paraparticles offer a new resource for quantum communication with unique security properties.

title: Gradient Scalability And Taylor Surrogation Of Quantum Cost Landscapes
authors: Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, And Aurelien Lucchi
abstract:
Author(s): Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, and Aurelien Lucchi

Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) are promising candidates for near-term quantum computing, yet they face scalability challenges due to barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially in the system size. Recent conjectures suggest that avoiding barren plateaus might inherently lead to clas…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023325] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the scalability of gradients in variational quantum algorithms and proposes a Taylor surrogation method to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus where gradients vanish exponentially, hindering scalability. The authors aim to understand the conditions under which gradients remain trainable and propose a method to avoid plateaus.
method: The authors analyze gradient scaling in parameterized quantum circuits and introduce a Taylor surrogation technique that approximates the cost function locally to provide non-vanishing gradients.
result: They show that avoiding barren plateaus may lead to classical simulability, but their Taylor surrogation method can improve trainability without sacrificing quantum advantage in certain regimes.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between gradient scalability and classical simulability, offering a practical approach to enhance VQA training.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Lieb-Mattis states are used for robust entangled differential phase sensing, offering common-mode noise rejection for quantum sensor networks.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for applications like atomic clocks and magnetometers, but is limited by common-mode noise. The authors aim to develop a scalable, noise-immune approach using entangled states.
method: The paper proposes using Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states of spin ensembles that are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode phase shifts, and analyzes their performance for differential phase estimation.
result: Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase while being robust to common-mode noise, outperforming conventional entangled states like spin-squeezed states in noisy environments.
conclusion: Lieb-Mattis states provide a practical and scalable platform for quantum-enhanced differential sensing, with potential applications in quantum sensor networks.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical states in trapped-ion systems, demonstrated for squeezed and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are useful for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with a combination of laser pulses and engineered interactions to prepare arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical properties.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile toolbox for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, with applications in quantum information processing and metrology.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution over fiber.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers compatibility with standard telecom components but suffers from limited secret key rates and security proofs. The authors aim to overcome these limitations using discrete modulation and composable security analysis.
method: The protocol uses a discrete modulation scheme (e.g., QPSK) combined with a composable security proof based on the entropy accumulation theorem and numerical optimization of the secret key rate.
result: They achieve record-high secret key rates over fiber distances up to 50 km, with rigorous composable security against collective attacks.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that discrete-modulated CV-QKD can achieve high rates and practical security, bringing quantum networks closer to real-world deployment.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms, demonstrating a key capability for quantum networking and computing.
conclusion: This technique enables new possibilities for using circular Rydberg atoms in quantum information processing, particularly for quantum networks and hybrid systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for improving qubit readout.
motivation: Understanding how transmon qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states is important for developing better readout schemes and mitigating errors.
method: The authors probe transmon ionization dynamics using experimental techniques and theoretical modeling, focusing on multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions.
result: They reveal the mechanisms of transmon ionization, showing how qubits transition to highly excited states through multiphoton processes.
conclusion: These findings provide insights into qubit leakage and inform the design of more robust readout protocols for superconducting qubits.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubits, challenging quantum error correction even with radiation shielding.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, using a combination of qubit measurements and noise analysis.
result: They identify a new type of correlated phase error burst that occurs even with state-of-the-art radiation protection, undermining error correction performance.
conclusion: Radiation-induced correlated errors pose a significant challenge for superconducting qubit arrays, requiring new mitigation strategies for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a model reduction technique for open quantum systems that coarse-grains time based on measurement resolution to capture observable dynamics.
motivation: Complex open quantum systems are computationally expensive to simulate; a method to reduce model complexity while preserving dynamics relevant to measurements is needed.
method: Measurement-adapted time-coarse graining: the time resolution of measurement channels defines a coarse-graining scale, and the reduced model is constructed by integrating out fast degrees of freedom beyond that scale.
result: The technique accurately reproduces measurement outcomes of the full system with significantly fewer degrees of freedom, demonstrated on examples.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical tool for simulating open quantum systems in quantum thermodynamics and quantum information contexts where measurement resolution is finite.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and fundamental tests; trapped ions offer a clean platform for generating and exploiting spin-dependent squeezed states.
method: The authors theoretically propose and experimentally realize a protocol using trapped ions to create spin-dependent squeezed states via spin-motion coupling, then apply them to displacement sensing.
result: They achieve optimal sensitivity for displacement estimation, surpassing the standard quantum limit and approaching the Heisenberg limit.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with implications for quantum-enhanced metrology.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a clear operational measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by linking non-Gaussianity to resource requirements.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries and non-Gaussian operations needed to prepare a state, and derive its properties using symplectic geometry and phase-space formalism.
result: The symplectic rank provides a tight lower bound on the number of non-Gaussian operations required for state preparation, compression, and measurement, and is shown to be computable for certain classes of states.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, with implications for resource theory and quantum information processing in continuous-variable systems.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying sources of decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters in silicon are promising for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding the origins of decoherence is crucial for improving coherence times.
method: The authors study single erbium ions coupled to silicon nanocavities, performing spectroscopy and noise analysis to characterize spectral diffusion and decoherence mechanisms.
result: They identify charge noise and phonon interactions as dominant sources of spectral instability, and demonstrate that cavity coupling can mitigate some decoherence.
conclusion: Cavity-enhanced erbium emitters in silicon can achieve improved spectral stability, making them viable for quantum networking and computation applications.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and not scalable.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over models and parameters, enabling fast and scalable estimation.
result: The method accurately identifies spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, outperforming standard approaches in efficiency.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides a practical tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions leading to blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays give rise to exotic non-equilibrium phenomena such as blockaded ferromagnetism and quantum scars.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, analyzing the interplay of long-range interactions and kinetic constraints using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that kinetic constraints stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating a new mechanism for non-thermal states in open quantum systems.
conclusion: The work establishes cavity QED with Rydberg atoms as a platform for exploring kinetically constrained many-body physics and long-range quantum correlations.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing requires high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse optimization framework that designs and optimizes multiqubit Rydberg gates, leveraging the Rydberg blockade mechanism.
result: The optimized gates achieve high fidelities suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrating the feasibility of multiqubit operations in neutral-atom systems.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing with neutral atoms by enabling efficient multiqubit gates.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work explores collective effects to achieve blockade with weaker coupling.
method: The authors theoretically study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the photon statistics and transmission using a master equation approach.
result: They find that the photon blockade effect is collectively enhanced with system size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving is a technique to speed up adiabatic quantum processes, but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from limited fidelity.
method: The authors introduce a weighted action approach combined with computer algebra to systematically optimize variational counterdiabatic protocols, enabling higher-fidelity control.
result: The new method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in benchmark examples.
conclusion: This work provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and quantum speed limits.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification and transduction of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved Josephson mixers are promising components for scalable quantum information processing and quantum networks.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation on neutral-atom platforms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires fault-tolerant architectures that minimize space and time overhead, especially for neutral-atom hardware where native gates and error models differ from superconducting qubits.
method: The authors design a transversal logical gate set tailored to neutral-atom hardware, incorporating small-angle rotation error correction and extending it to high-rate quantum error-correcting codes. They analyze logical layout, space, and time overhead through detailed resource estimation.
result: The proposed architecture achieves significant savings in logical qubit count and execution time compared to standard surface-code approaches, enabling megaquop-scale simulations within realistic hardware constraints.
conclusion: Neutral-atom quantum computers can efficiently support fault-tolerant quantum simulation with a transversal architecture, making them a promising platform for practical quantum advantage.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is central to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques to solve the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem efficiently.
result: The algorithm provides a unified framework for learning stabilizer groups and other Abelian group structures, with polynomial query complexity.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory by generalizing the hidden subgroup problem to a state setting, with implications for quantum learning and cryptography.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without adding noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This work provides a new method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, enabling significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine for many quantum algorithms, but its resource requirements are often prohibitive due to the need for precise Hamiltonian simulation.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized product formulas that combine deterministic and randomized Trotter steps to reduce the effective circuit depth while maintaining accuracy.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard Trotter-based phase estimation.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution offers a practical and efficient approach to implementing phase estimation on near-term quantum devices.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurement fidelity in multilevel quantum systems, demonstrated on a silicon spin qudit.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems often cause backaction that destroys quantum information; a nondemolition readout is crucial for quantum error correction and state preparation.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis to minimize backaction, using real-time feedback on a silicon spin qudit.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors.
conclusion: Adaptive readout is a practical technique to enhance nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, applicable across various qudit platforms.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental implementations.
motivation: Continuous-variable approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure and higher detection efficiencies.
method: The review surveys theoretical foundations (Gaussian states, homodyne detection, reconciliation) and experimental progress in CV-QKD, entanglement distribution, and quantum networks.
result: CV quantum communication is now a mature field with record distances and rates, and is a leading candidate for scalable quantum networks.
conclusion: Continuous-variable techniques are essential for practical quantum communication and will play a key role in future quantum networks.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To classify and assess the security of quantum cryptographic protocols that go beyond key distribution, highlighting their potential and limitations.
method: The paper provides a systematic classification of quantum cryptographic primitives, discusses their security definitions, and reviews experimental implementations using photonic platforms.
result: It presents a taxonomy of quantum crypto primitives, explains their security guarantees and limitations, and surveys current photonic experiments.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers enhanced security for many tasks beyond QKD, but practical implementations face challenges; the field is ripe for further theoretical and experimental advances.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory with focus on symmetry, topology, and purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors use nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify stationary states and universal scaling, incorporating symmetry and topology.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open matter, linking to quantum state purity and topological features.
conclusion: The review provides a systematic classification that guides future experiments and theory in nonequilibrium quantum thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques for spin-spin relaxation times.
motivation: Understanding and predicting decoherence is crucial for developing long-coherence spin qubits, which are key for quantum technologies.
method: The paper reviews ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times for various spin qubit platforms.
result: Cluster expansion techniques can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubits, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming reliable, aiding the design of better spin qubits, though further work is needed for complex environments.

title: Superbunching From Coherently Driven Atoms In A Waveguide
authors: Zeidan Zeidan, Therese Karmstrand, Maryam Khanahmadi, And Göran Johansson
abstract:
Author(s): Zeidan Zeidan, Therese Karmstrand, Maryam Khanahmadi, and Göran Johansson

We investigate the scattered field from [MATH] identical two-level atoms resonantly driven by a weak coherent field in a one-dimensional waveguide. For atoms separated by the drive wavelength, increasing the number of atoms suppresses transmission while enhancing photon bunching. Transmission becomes a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250803] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Coherently driven atoms in a waveguide exhibit superbunching and suppressed transmission as atom number increases.
motivation: Understanding photon statistics from many-atom systems in waveguides is important for quantum optics and quantum network applications.
method: The authors theoretically study N two-level atoms coupled to a 1D waveguide, driven by a weak coherent field, and compute the scattered field correlation functions.
result: Increasing the number of atoms enhances photon bunching (g^(2)(0) grows superlinearly) and suppresses transmission, leading to superbunching.
conclusion: The effect arises from collective atomic responses and could be used for generating non-classical light or probing many-body physics in waveguide QED.

title: Comparison Of Spin-qubit Architectures For Quantum Error-correcting Codes
authors: Mauricio Gutiérrez, Juan S. Rojas-Arias, David Obando, And Chien-Yuan Chang
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio Gutiérrez, Juan S. Rojas-Arias, David Obando, and Chien-Yuan Chang

We investigate the performance of two quantum error-correcting codes—the surface code and the Bacon-Shor code—for implementation with spin qubits in silicon. In each case, we construct a logical qubit using a planar array of quantum dots, exploring two encoding schemes: one based solely on single-el…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062464] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Compares surface code and Bacon-Shor code performance on spin qubit architectures in silicon quantum dots.
motivation: To identify which quantum error-correcting code is best suited for spin qubit platforms, considering physical constraints like limited connectivity and noise.
method: Constructs logical qubits using planar quantum dot arrays with two encoding schemes (single-electron and singlet-triplet), and simulates logical error rates under realistic noise models.
result: The Bacon-Shor code outperforms the surface code for the considered spin qubit architectures due to lower overhead and better tolerance to specific noise channels.
conclusion: Architecture-aware code selection is crucial for practical quantum error correction with spin qubits.

title: Identifying Emergent Spin Excitations Through Correlation Structures
authors: Fan Xia, Xin-Yu Pan, Gang-Qin Liu, And Ping Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Fan Xia, Xin-Yu Pan, Gang-Qin Liu, and Ping Wang

Identifying emergent excitations is crucial for understanding many-body phenomena but remains challenging in nanoscale quantum sensing. Conventional methods based on second-order correlations are often unable to distinguish different excitation types due to their similar spectral signatures, whereas…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062623] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a method to identify emergent spin excitations in many-body systems using higher-order correlation functions, demonstrated with NV centers.
motivation: Conventional second-order correlations fail to distinguish different excitation types in nanoscale quantum sensing; higher-order correlations can resolve this.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework using third- and fourth-order correlation functions and simulate detection with NV center sensors.
result: Higher-order correlations provide clear signatures to differentiate magnons, spinons, and other excitations, even when spectral features overlap.
conclusion: This approach enhances the capability of quantum sensors to characterize emergent excitations in condensed matter systems.

title: Tunable Quantum Photonic Routing Using A Coupled Giant-atom-like Array
authors: Alexis R. Legón, Mario Miranda, And P. A. Orellana
abstract:
Author(s): Alexis R. Legón, Mario Miranda, and P. A. Orellana

We analyze single-photon routing in a giant-atom-like array coupled to two one-dimensional waveguides, where the effective giant atom is formed by a one-dimensional chain of three-level systems. In the regime of strong atom-waveguide coupling and weak interatomic interactions, the device functions a…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063531] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of single-photon routing using a giant-atom-like array coupled to two waveguides, demonstrating tunable routing via interatomic interactions.
motivation: To design a controllable quantum photonic router for quantum networks, leveraging giant-atom effects and waveguide QED.
method: Analyzes a one-dimensional chain of three-level systems (giant-atom-like array) coupled to two waveguides, using master equation and scattering theory in the strong coupling regime.
result: The device functions as a tunable router where the routing direction and efficiency can be controlled by interatomic interactions and detuning.
conclusion: The proposed giant-atom-like array provides a feasible platform for quantum photonic routing, relevant for quantum network applications.

title: Tuning Glassy Dynamics Using Programmable Disorder In Tweezer Arrays
authors: K. Mukherjee, G. W. Biedermann, And R. J. Lewis-Swan
abstract:
Author(s): K. Mukherjee, G. W. Biedermann, and R. J. Lewis-Swan

We propose a unifying framework for nonequilibrium relaxation dynamics in ensembles of positionally disordered interacting quantum spins based on the statistical properties, such as mean and variance, of the underlying disorder distribution. Our framework is validated through extensive exact numeric…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061302] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A framework for tuning glassy dynamics in disordered quantum spin ensembles using programmable disorder distributions.
motivation: Understanding nonequilibrium relaxation in disordered quantum systems is important for quantum simulation and information processing.
method: The authors develop a statistical framework based on the mean and variance of the disorder distribution, validated by exact numerical simulations of spin models in tweezer arrays.
result: They show that the relaxation dynamics can be systematically controlled by engineering the disorder distribution, enabling tunable glassy behavior.
conclusion: Programmable disorder in tweezer arrays provides a versatile platform for studying and controlling glassy dynamics, with implications for quantum memory and thermalization.

title: Quantum Implementation Of Higher-order Power Method For Estimating Geometric Entanglement Of Pure States
authors: Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, And Elena Blokhina
abstract:
Author(s): Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, and Elena Blokhina

Entanglement is one of the fundamental properties of a quantum state and is a crucial differentiator between classical and quantum computation. There are many ways to define entanglement and its measure, depending on the problem or application under consideration. Each of these measures may be compu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062459] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A quantum algorithm for estimating geometric entanglement of pure states using the higher-order power method.
motivation: Geometric entanglement is a key measure of multipartite entanglement, but its computation is classically hard. A quantum implementation could enable efficient estimation on near-term quantum devices.
method: The authors propose a quantum circuit that implements the higher-order power method to find the closest separable state and compute the geometric measure of entanglement for pure states.
result: The algorithm is analyzed in terms of circuit depth and qubit requirements, showing polynomial scaling with system size for certain states, and demonstrated on small examples.
conclusion: The quantum implementation offers a potential speedup for estimating geometric entanglement, though practical realization depends on hardware improvements.

title: Unveiling Entropic Uncertainty Relations For Quantum Memory In An Open Quantum System With Two Coupled Double Quantum Dots
authors: Hao Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Wang

In this work, we investigate quantum correlations, the quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relation (QMA-EUR), and its lower bound in a system with two coupled double quantum dots, where each coupled double quantum dot interacts independently with its own infinite-dimensional bosonic reserv…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062460] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Investigates quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relations in a system of two coupled double quantum dots interacting with bosonic reservoirs.
motivation: To understand how open quantum system dynamics affect entropic uncertainty relations, which are fundamental to quantum information processing and cryptography.
method: The study models two coupled double quantum dots, each coupled to its own bosonic reservoir, and computes the QMA-EUR and its lower bound using quantum correlation measures.
result: The entropic uncertainty and its lower bound are influenced by inter-dot coupling, reservoir temperature, and initial state correlations, with quantum correlations playing a key role.
conclusion: The work provides insights into controlling uncertainty in open quantum systems, relevant for quantum memory and secure communication protocols.

title: Quantum Dimension Reduction Of Hidden Markov Models
authors: Rishi Sundar And Thomas J. Elliott
abstract:
Author(s): Rishi Sundar and Thomas J. Elliott

Hidden Markov models (HMMs) are ubiquitous in time-series modeling, with applications ranging from chemical reaction modeling to speech recognition. These HMMs are often large, with high-dimensional memories. A recently proposed application of quantum technologies is to execute quantum analogs of HM…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062461] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum dimension reduction technique for hidden Markov models using quantum information theory, achieving exponential memory savings.
motivation: Hidden Markov models often require large classical memory; quantum analogs can reduce memory via quantum superposition and entanglement.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that compresses the classical memory of an HMM into a quantum system of lower dimension, leveraging quantum state compression and quantum information measures.
result: They demonstrate that the quantum dimension reduction can achieve exponential reduction in memory size compared to classical HMMs, with rigorous bounds on approximation error.
conclusion: Quantum dimension reduction offers a practical advantage for simulating large HMMs, with potential applications in time-series analysis and machine learning.

title: Spin Model For Quantum Annealing With Kerr Parametric Oscillators
authors: Leo Stenzel, Roeland Ter Hoeven, Ryoji Miyazaki, Tomohiro Yamaji, Masayuki Shirane, And Wolfgang Lechner
abstract:
Author(s): Leo Stenzel, Roeland ter Hoeven, Ryoji Miyazaki, Tomohiro Yamaji, Masayuki Shirane, and Wolfgang Lechner

Coherent states offer a promising path for near-term quantum computing due to their inherent protection against bit-flip noise. However, their large photon numbers can be challenging for numerical simulation. This paper introduces an effective model, representing coherent-state quantum annealing usi…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062621] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Introduces an effective spin model for quantum annealing using Kerr parametric oscillators, enabling efficient simulation of coherent-state quantum annealing.
motivation: Coherent-state quantum annealing with Kerr parametric oscillators is promising for near-term quantum computing but challenging to simulate due to large photon numbers; an effective model is needed.
method: Derives an effective spin model that captures the essential physics of the coherent-state annealing process, reducing computational complexity.
result: The effective model accurately reproduces the dynamics and performance of the full system, enabling larger-scale simulations.
conclusion: The spin model provides a practical tool for studying quantum annealing with Kerr parametric oscillators, advancing hybrid quantum systems for optimization.

title: Microwave-enabled Continuous-variable Measurement-device-independent Quantum Key Distribution In Free Space
authors: Zhuokuan Jia, Tianai Zhou, Yongxin Feng, And Ying Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Zhuokuan Jia, Tianai Zhou, Yongxin Feng, and Ying Guo

Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) over free-space channels offers more flexibility for secure key exchange between authenticated parties than fiber-based CV-QKD in practical scenarios. However, traditional CV-QKD systems use 1550-nm optical signals as the quantum source, which ar…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062450] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a microwave-enabled continuous-variable measurement-device-independent QKD protocol for free-space channels to overcome atmospheric attenuation.
motivation: Free-space CV-QKD at 1550 nm suffers from atmospheric attenuation; using microwave frequencies can reduce losses and enable longer-distance secure key exchange.
method: The authors design a CV-MDI-QKD protocol using microwave signals instead of optical, analyze the security against collective attacks, and simulate key rates under realistic free-space channel conditions.
result: The microwave-based protocol achieves higher secret key rates and longer transmission distances compared to optical CV-MDI-QKD in free space, especially under adverse weather.
conclusion: Microwave-enabled CV-MDI-QKD is a promising approach for practical free-space quantum communication, offering improved performance over traditional optical implementations.

title: Generalized Stochastic Spin-wave Theory For Open Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Zejian Li, Anna Delmonte, And Rosario Fazio
abstract:
Author(s): Zejian Li, Anna Delmonte, and Rosario Fazio

We propose a semiclassical framework for solving open quantum dynamics in driven-dissipative spin systems. Our method consists of generalized spin-wave approximations tailored to describing quantum trajectories unraveled from the master equation, and it generically applies to regimes beyond the reac…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214324] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical framework for simulating open quantum spin systems using generalized spin-wave theory and quantum trajectories.
motivation: Open quantum spin systems are important for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information, but exact simulations are computationally expensive; a semiclassical method can capture dissipative dynamics efficiently.
method: The authors develop generalized spin-wave approximations that describe quantum trajectories unraveled from the master equation, applicable beyond the reaction coordinate regime.
result: The framework provides accurate approximations for driven-dissipative spin systems, validated against exact solutions in certain limits.
conclusion: This semiclassical approach offers a scalable tool for studying open quantum systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium dynamics.

title: Dynamics Of Majorana Fermions On A Quantum Computer
authors: Yuxiao Hang, Rosa Di Felice, Aiichiro Nakano, And Stephan Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Yuxiao Hang, Rosa Di Felice, Aiichiro Nakano, and Stephan Haas

The study of quasiparticle dynamics is central to understanding nonequilibrium phenomena in quantum many-body systems. Direct simulation of such dynamics on quantum hardware has been limited by circuit depth and noise constraints. In this work, we use a recently developed constant-depth circuit algo…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235145] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Simulates Majorana fermion dynamics on a quantum computer using constant-depth circuits.
motivation: Understanding quasiparticle dynamics in quantum many-body systems is limited by circuit depth and noise; this work aims to overcome these constraints.
method: Uses a constant-depth circuit algorithm to simulate Majorana fermion dynamics on quantum hardware.
result: Demonstrates feasible simulation of Majorana dynamics with reduced circuit depth, enabling study of nonequilibrium phenomena.
conclusion: Constant-depth circuits offer a practical path to simulating complex quasiparticle dynamics on near-term quantum computers.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: Lessons From Active And Passive Stochastic Dynamics
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of parity and time-reversal symmetries as necessary for the emergence of steady-state directed currents. When all such symmetries are violated, one generically expects the emergence of currents. We study stochastic systems in the presence of asymmetri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064152] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper revisits the ratchet principle in stochastic systems, showing that directed currents can emerge even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are preserved, through active or passive asymmetric potentials.
motivation: To clarify the necessary conditions for directed transport in stochastic systems, challenging the traditional ratchet principle that requires violation of both parity and time-reversal symmetries.
method: The authors analyze stochastic dynamics with asymmetric potentials, both in active (self-propelled particles) and passive (thermal) settings, using theoretical models and simulations.
result: They demonstrate that directed currents can arise even when all symmetries are preserved, provided the system is out of equilibrium due to activity or non-thermal noise.
conclusion: The ratchet principle must be refined: violation of parity and time-reversal is sufficient but not necessary for directed transport; non-equilibrium conditions alone can suffice.

title: Minimal-dissipation Learning For Energy-based Models
authors: Jeff Hnybida And Simon Verret
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Hnybida and Simon Verret

We show that the bias of the approximate maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE) objective of a persistent chain energy-based model (EBM) is precisely equal to the thermodynamic excess work of an overdamped Langevin dynamical system. We then answer the question of whether such a model can be trained wit…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065306] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that the bias in maximum-likelihood estimation for energy-based models equals thermodynamic excess work, and explores minimal-dissipation training.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic cost of training energy-based models and to find training protocols that minimize dissipation.
method: The authors map the training dynamics of persistent chain energy-based models to an overdamped Langevin system and compute the excess work using stochastic thermodynamics.
result: The bias of approximate MLE is exactly the thermodynamic excess work, and they derive conditions for minimal-dissipation learning.
conclusion: Energy-based models can be trained with minimal thermodynamic cost by controlling the learning rate schedule, connecting machine learning to thermodynamics.

title: Dynamical Typicality In Classical Lattice Systems
authors: Nicolas Nessi And Peter Reimann
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Nessi and Peter Reimann

Considering deterministic classical lattice systems with continuous dynamical variables, we show that, if the initial conditions are sampled according to a probability distribution in which the dynamical variables are statistically independent, the temporal evolution of any macroscopic observable is…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064138] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Shows that dynamical typicality holds for classical lattice systems with independent initial conditions, meaning macroscopic observables evolve close to their microcanonical average for most initial states.
motivation: To extend the concept of dynamical typicality, previously studied in quantum systems, to classical lattice systems, providing a rigorous foundation for equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: Analytical proof using probability theory and ergodic theory for deterministic classical lattice systems with continuous variables and independent initial distributions.
result: For any macroscopic observable, the time evolution from typical initial conditions is close to the microcanonical ensemble average, with deviations bounded by system size.
conclusion: Dynamical typicality is a general property of classical lattice systems, supporting the emergence of thermodynamic behavior from deterministic dynamics.

title: Diffusion In Quantum State Preparation: From Passive Cooling To System-bath Engineering
authors: Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, and Jan Carl Budich

We investigate and compare two particle number-conserving protocols for the preparation of a topologically nontrivial state. The first is derived from thermally coupling the system to a cold bath, while the second is based on engineered dissipation. We numerically study the time required to reach th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023336] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Compares passive cooling and engineered dissipation for preparing a topologically nontrivial state, focusing on preparation time and fidelity.
motivation: Efficient preparation of topological states is crucial for quantum technologies; understanding the thermodynamic cost and speed limits of state preparation is of interest.
method: Numerical simulation of two particle number-conserving protocols: one based on thermal coupling to a cold bath, the other on engineered dissipation.
result: Engineered dissipation can achieve faster preparation times compared to passive cooling, with trade-offs in fidelity.
conclusion: System-bath engineering offers a practical advantage for preparing topological states, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Casimir-Polder Potential On An Excited Atom Near An Atomic Array
authors: Annyun Das And Kanu Sinha
abstract:
Author(s): Annyun Das and Kanu Sinha

We develop a microscopic description of the fluctuation-mediated Casimir-Polder (CP) shifts on a “test” two-level atom placed near a two-dimensional atomic array of two-level atoms. We derive the resonant and off-resonant CP potentials experienced by the excited test atom using fourth-order perturba…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023339] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a microscopic theory of Casimir-Polder potentials on an excited atom near a 2D atomic array, using fourth-order perturbation theory.
motivation: Understanding fluctuation-mediated interactions between quantum emitters and atomic arrays is important for hybrid quantum systems and quantum networks.
method: The authors use fourth-order perturbation theory to derive resonant and off-resonant Casimir-Polder potentials for a test two-level atom near a two-dimensional atomic array of two-level atoms.
result: They obtain expressions for the CP potential that include both resonant and off-resonant contributions, showing how the array modifies the atom's environment.
conclusion: The work provides a microscopic foundation for Casimir-Polder interactions in atomic arrays, relevant for controlling atom-array interactions in quantum technologies.

title: Rotation Sensor Based On An Atom-cavity System
authors: Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, And Ludwig Mathey
abstract:
Author(s): Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, and Ludwig Mathey

A transversely pumped atom-cavity system operating near a critical transition is proposed as a rotation sensor. The cavity-emitted light serves as a probe for changes in rotation frequency, with a sensitivity that scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022057] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an atom-cavity system as a rotation sensor with sensitivity scaling with the enclosed area.
motivation: To develop a quantum-enhanced rotation sensor using a transversely pumped atom-cavity system operating near a critical transition.
method: The system uses cavity-emitted light as a probe to detect changes in rotation frequency, leveraging the critical transition for enhanced sensitivity.
result: The sensitivity scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array, demonstrating a quantum advantage in rotation sensing.
conclusion: The atom-cavity system provides a promising platform for high-precision rotation sensing, relevant to quantum metrology and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Dynamical Signatures Of Topological Flow Transitions In Limit Cycle Phases
authors: Alejandro S. Gómez And Javier Del Pino
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro S. Gómez and Javier del Pino

Quantum self-oscillatory phases are ubiquitous in driven-dissipative systems. Classically, each phase is defined by its flow pattern and how stationary sets organize phase space (e.g., fixed points and limit cycles), with transitions triggered by local bifurcations or global basin rearrangements. In…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023319] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum signatures of topological flow transitions in limit cycle phases of driven-dissipative systems, linking classical bifurcations to quantum observables.
motivation: Understanding how classical topological features of phase space (limit cycles, flow patterns) manifest in quantum systems is crucial for characterizing driven-dissipative phases and their transitions.
method: The authors analyze a quantum van der Pol oscillator model using phase-space methods and quantum trajectory simulations to compute dynamical signatures such as power spectra and correlation functions.
result: They identify distinct quantum signatures that signal topological flow transitions, including changes in the spectral line shape and correlation decay rates, which can be observed experimentally.
conclusion: Quantum systems retain classical flow topology near the semiclassical limit, and these signatures provide a way to detect bifurcations in quantum self-oscillatory phases.

title: Memory-enhanced Quantum Extreme Learning Machines For Characterizing non-Markovian Dynamics
authors: Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, And Gian Luca Giorgi
abstract:
Author(s): Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, and Gian Luca Giorgi

We use a quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) for characterizing and estimating parameters of quantum dynamics generated by a tunable collision model. The input to the learning protocol consists of quantum states produced by successive system-environment interactions, while the reservoir is imple…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023306] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses a quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) with memory to characterize non-Markovian dynamics in a collision model, demonstrating parameter estimation and detection of non-Markovianity.
motivation: Characterizing non-Markovian quantum dynamics is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are often computationally expensive. Machine learning offers a more efficient approach.
method: A QELM is implemented using a reservoir of qubits with memory (via feedback loops) to process input states from a collision model. The reservoir's output is used to estimate parameters of the system-environment interaction and detect non-Markovianity.
result: The memory-enhanced QELM successfully estimates the system-environment coupling strength and the degree of non-Markovianity with high accuracy, outperforming standard QELMs without memory.
conclusion: Memory-enhanced QELMs are effective tools for characterizing non-Markovian dynamics, with potential applications in quantum metrology and quantum control.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A review of the process tensor framework for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics using tensor-network methods.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are important in many quantum systems but are computationally challenging; efficient simulation methods are needed.
method: The paper reviews the process tensor formalism and shows how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable practical simulation of complex open quantum systems.
result: The framework can capture non-Markovian memory effects and is applied to various physical systems, demonstrating scalability and accuracy.
conclusion: Process tensor approaches with tensor networks provide a powerful tool for studying non-Markovian quantum dynamics, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and open systems.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensates can process information through phase transitions, linking physical chemistry to cellular computation.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals, but traditional molecular pathways may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, high-dimensional information processing mechanism.
method: The authors present a conceptual framework drawing on phase separation, multi-component condensates, and analogies to neural networks and thermodynamic computing.
result: They argue that condensates can classify signals, perform analog computations, and implement memory via hysteresis, with phase boundaries acting as decision thresholds.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation provides a plausible physical substrate for cellular information processing, suggesting new directions for synthetic biology and thermodynamic computing.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect, using truncated propagators.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze the dynamics of quantum circuits and compute thermalization times.
result: Shadowing time is finite in many-body chaotic systems, and the Trotterization transition disappears in the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: The findings clarify the nature of prethermalization and have implications for quantum simulation and thermalization in driven systems.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally challenging; photonic platforms offer scalability and reconfigurability.
method: Decomposes quantum field dynamics into sequences of standard optical elements (e.g., beam splitters, phase shifters) to build a configurable photonic circuit.
result: Demonstrates efficient simulation of a class of quantum field theories with high configurational flexibility.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical path toward analog quantum simulation of field theories using integrated photonics.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits at finite depths, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Anticoncentration is a key property for quantum advantage and random circuit sampling, but its behavior under noise is not well understood. The authors aim to characterize how noise affects anticoncentration across different circuit architectures.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework using statistical mechanics mappings and replica methods to analyze the output distribution of noisy random circuits. They consider various noise models and circuit topologies.
result: They find that anticoncentration persists up to a depth-dependent noise threshold, with a universal scaling that is independent of circuit architecture. The transition between anticoncentrated and concentrated regimes is described by a universal function.
conclusion: The results provide a unified understanding of anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits, with implications for benchmarking and verifying quantum computers.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
