authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but loading and imaging them with high fidelity and low loss remains challenging. Existing methods often cause atom loss or require destructive measurements.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve nondestructive imaging and loading of atom arrays. They use a probe-pump scheme in a finite magnetic field to enhance imaging contrast and reduce scattering-induced loss.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity imaging with low atom loss and efficient loading of continuously operated arrays, achieving improved performance over standard techniques.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading provide a practical, high-performance method for neutral-atom arrays, advancing their use in quantum information processing and simulation.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit platforms is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible intermediate-frequency regime.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations from single-shot measurements, demonstrating its effectiveness on a qubit platform.
conclusion: This technique provides a new tool for noise characterization in qubit systems, which can aid in understanding decoherence and improving qubit performance.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling sequences for multi-qubit systems often scale poorly with qubit number; this work aims to design efficient sequences that cancel k-local noise.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, leveraging code properties to achieve simultaneous decoupling of all k-local error terms.
result: They produce device-tailored sequences whose length depends only on the locality k and not on the total number of qubits, enabling practical implementation in large systems.
conclusion: This approach bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering a scalable method to combat correlated noise in quantum devices.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size. Understanding how noise affects loss function concentration is crucial for practical training.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the variance of the loss function under noise, relating it to the expressivity of the circuit measured by the dimension of the dynamical Lie algebra.
result: They show that noise can reduce the variance of the loss function, potentially alleviating barren plateaus, and provide quantitative estimates of concentration depending on noise strength and circuit expressivity.
conclusion: The results offer a principled way to navigate barren plateaus by balancing noise and expressivity, guiding the design of trainable variational quantum circuits.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for quantum simulation and non-equilibrium dynamics, with potential implications for quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical models and numerical simulations, likely including tensor networks or exact diagonalization, to study the dynamics of string breaking in a quantum spin chain or lattice gauge theory.
result: They identify experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits rich quantum dynamics, including diabatic effects and non-adiabatic transitions.
conclusion: The work provides new probes for string breaking and highlights the role of quantum dynamics in confining systems, relevant for quantum simulators and thermodynamic processes.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations improves simulation accuracy by sevenfold for variational algorithms.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse noise model capturing spatiotemporally correlated errors using a combination of experimental characterization and theoretical fitting.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms compared to standard Markovian models.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise models are effective for capturing complex error correlations in transmon processors, enabling better simulation and error mitigation.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors in exchange-only spin qubits degrade gate fidelity; protecting idle operation is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons to be exactly equal, opening an energy gap between the computational subspace and leakage states.
result: They achieve suppressed leakage errors during idle operation, improving qubit coherence and fidelity.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical method to mitigate leakage in exchange-only spin qubits, advancing their viability for quantum information processing.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum technologies, but the diversity of simulation methods makes it hard to compare and choose approaches.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and use it to categorize and compare various simulation techniques (e.g., hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, tensor networks).
result: The review provides a clear taxonomy of methods, highlighting their commonalities, differences, and regimes of applicability, with examples from quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
conclusion: The unified framework helps researchers select appropriate simulation tools for non-Markovian open quantum systems, advancing both theoretical understanding and practical applications.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms more efficiently.
motivation: Qubits are standard but qudits can reduce gate complexity and resource requirements for certain quantum operations, such as the Toffoli gate.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decomposition techniques using qudits, and reviews experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits enable simpler decompositions of multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli gate with a single qutrit) and offer potential advantages in quantum algorithm realization.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum computing, though practical challenges remain; further research is needed to fully exploit their benefits.

title: Dissipative Phase Transition Of Interacting Nonreciprocal Fermions
authors: Rafael D. Soares, Matteo Brunelli, And Marco Schirò
abstract:
Author(s): Rafael D. Soares, Matteo Brunelli, and Marco Schirò

While nonreciprocal couplings are ubiquitous in classical systems, their impact on quantum many-body criticality and entanglement remains largely unexplored. Using exact numerical simulations, we study an interacting fermionic chain subject to nonreciprocal gain and loss. We show that the interplay …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250403] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dissipative phase transition in an interacting fermionic chain with nonreciprocal gain and loss, focusing on criticality and entanglement.
motivation: Nonreciprocal couplings are common in classical systems but their impact on quantum many-body criticality and entanglement is largely unexplored.
method: Exact numerical simulations of an interacting fermionic chain with nonreciprocal gain and loss.
result: The interplay of nonreciprocity and interactions leads to a dissipative phase transition with distinct entanglement properties.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal couplings can fundamentally alter quantum critical behavior and entanglement, opening new avenues for exploring non-Hermitian many-body physics.

title: Black Hole Thermodynamics Without Black Hole Solutions
authors: Meng-Nan Yang, Guan-Yi Lu, And H. Lü
abstract:
Author(s): Meng-Nan Yang, Guan-Yi Lu, and H. Lü

We consider the string-theory-inspired Einstein-Maxwell-Maxwell-dilaton theory and show that we can derive the complete set of thermodynamic quantities of charged black holes without having to construct the black hole solutions. We argue that the technique can be applied more broadly to string theor…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251403] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A method to derive black hole thermodynamics without solving the field equations, using a general technique applicable to string-inspired theories.
motivation: Black hole thermodynamics is typically derived from explicit solutions, which can be cumbersome. The authors aim to extract thermodynamic quantities directly from the Lagrangian and symmetries.
method: They use the Einstein-Maxwell-Maxwell-dilaton theory and apply a scaling argument or Wald-like formalism to compute entropy, temperature, and charges without constructing the metric.
result: They successfully reproduce the thermodynamic quantities of charged black holes in this theory, demonstrating the technique's validity.
conclusion: The approach can be generalized to other string-theory-inspired gravity theories, simplifying thermodynamic analysis.

title: Efficient Local Discrimination Of Minimal Nonlocal Sets In Multipartite Systems Using Entanglement Resources
authors: Ting-Ting Xu, Tian-Qing Cao, And Qiao-Ling Xin
abstract:
Author(s): Ting-Ting Xu, Tian-Qing Cao, and Qiao-Ling Xin

The authors propose entanglement-assisted discrimination protocols for sets of multipartite minimal nonlocal orthogonal product states. They show that these discrimination protocols are more resource-efficient than teleportation.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062465] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes entanglement-assisted protocols for locally discriminating minimal nonlocal sets of multipartite orthogonal product states, showing resource efficiency over teleportation.
motivation: To achieve efficient local discrimination of nonlocal sets of quantum states, which is fundamental for quantum communication and information processing.
method: The authors design discrimination protocols that use entanglement resources (e.g., Bell states) and compare their resource cost to teleportation-based approaches.
result: The entanglement-assisted protocols require fewer resources (e.g., fewer entangled pairs) than teleportation for discriminating certain minimal nonlocal sets.
conclusion: Entanglement assistance can improve the efficiency of local state discrimination, with potential applications in quantum communication and cryptography.

title: Rigorous No-go Theorems For Heralded Linear-optical State Generation Tasks
authors: Deepesh Singh, Ryan J. Marshman, Luis Villegas-Aguilar, Jens Eisert, And Nora Tischler
abstract:
Author(s): Deepesh Singh, Ryan J. Marshman, Luis Villegas-Aguilar, Jens Eisert, and Nora Tischler

A major challenge in photonic quantum technologies is developing strategies to prepare suitable discrete-variable quantum states using simple input states, linear optics, and auxiliary photon measurements to identify successful outcomes. Fundamentally, this challenge arises from the lack of strong n…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063735] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves no-go theorems for heralded linear-optical state generation, showing that certain non-Gaussian states cannot be produced with high success probability using linear optics and photon counting.
motivation: Photonic quantum technologies require reliable preparation of discrete-variable quantum states, but linear optics and heralding impose fundamental limitations that need to be understood.
method: The authors use resource-theoretic arguments and linear-optical constraints to derive bounds on the success probability of heralded state generation tasks.
result: They establish rigorous no-go theorems showing that for many target states, the success probability decays exponentially with the number of photons, even with optimal linear-optical circuits.
conclusion: These results highlight fundamental limitations of linear-optical quantum computing and suggest that nonlinear resources or alternative approaches are necessary for scalable photonic state preparation.

title: Efficient Circuit Compression By Multiqudit Entangling Gates In Linear Optical Quantum Computation
authors: Apurav Tehri And Jaskaran Singh
abstract:
Author(s): Apurav Tehri and Jaskaran Singh

Linear optical quantum computation (LOQC) offers a promising platform for quantum information processing, but its scalability is fundamentally constrained by the probabilistic nature of nonlocal entangling gates. Qudit circuit compression schemes mitigate this issue by encoding multiple qubits onto …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062622] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Proposes circuit compression using multiqudit entangling gates to reduce resource overhead in linear optical quantum computation.
motivation: Linear optical quantum computation faces scalability issues due to probabilistic entangling gates; qudit encoding can mitigate this by reducing the number of required operations.
method: The authors design multiqudit entangling gates that operate on qudits encoding multiple qubits, and analyze their efficiency in compressing quantum circuits.
result: The proposed scheme achieves significant reduction in gate count and resource overhead compared to standard qubit-based LOQC approaches.
conclusion: Multiqudit entangling gates offer a practical path toward more efficient LOQC, though experimental realization remains challenging.

title: Quantum Simulation Of Fermionic non-Abelian Lattice Gauge Theories In $(2+1)$ Dimensions With Built-in Gauge Protection
authors: Gaia de Paciani, Lukas Homeier, Jad C. Halimeh, Monika Aidelsburger, And Fabian Grusdt
abstract:
Author(s): Gaia De Paciani, Lukas Homeier, Jad C. Halimeh, Monika Aidelsburger, and Fabian Grusdt

Recent advancements in the field of quantum simulation have significantly expanded the potential for applications, particularly in the context of lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Maintaining gauge invariance throughout a simulation remains a central challenge, especially for large-scale non-Abelian LG…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063327] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum simulation scheme for non-Abelian lattice gauge theories in (2+1)D with built-in gauge protection using ultracold atoms in optical lattices.
motivation: Simulating non-Abelian lattice gauge theories is challenging due to gauge invariance violations; the authors aim to design a scheme that inherently protects gauge symmetry.
method: They design a Hamiltonian with local gauge constraints using ultracold fermionic atoms in an optical lattice, employing a combination of hopping and interaction terms that enforce Gauss's law.
result: The scheme achieves robust gauge invariance without active error correction, and numerical simulations show accurate dynamics for small systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a scalable path to quantum simulate non-Abelian gauge theories, relevant for high-energy physics and condensed matter.

title: Accelerated Spin-adapted Ground-state Preparation With Nonvariational Quantum Algorithms
authors: Takumi Kobori, Taichi Kosugi, Hirofumi Nishi, Synge Todo, And Yu-Ichiro Matsushita
abstract:
Author(s): Takumi Kobori, Taichi Kosugi, Hirofumi Nishi, Synge Todo, and Yu-ichiro Matsushita

Various methods have been explored to prepare the spin-adapted ground state—the lowest energy state within the Hilbert space constrained by externally specified values of the total spin magnitude and the spin-[MATH] component. In such problem settings, nonvariational methods incorporate penalty terms i…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062454] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a nonvariational quantum algorithm for preparing spin-adapted ground states using penalty terms and quantum phase estimation.
motivation: Preparing ground states with specific spin symmetry is important for quantum chemistry and condensed matter physics, but existing variational methods may suffer from optimization issues.
method: The authors introduce a nonvariational approach that incorporates penalty terms to enforce spin constraints and uses quantum phase estimation to project onto the ground state within the desired spin subspace.
result: The method accelerates ground-state preparation compared to standard variational algorithms, as demonstrated on small molecular systems.
conclusion: Nonvariational quantum algorithms can efficiently prepare spin-adapted ground states, offering a practical advantage for near-term quantum devices.

title: Identifying The Three-qubit $w$ State With The Quantum Uncertainty Relation
authors: Zhi-Jie Liu, Hao-Nan Qiang, Jie Zhou, Mi Xie, And Jing-Ling Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Jie Liu, Hao-Nan Qiang, Jie Zhou, Mi Xie, and Jing-Ling Chen

The [MATH] state, a canonical representative of multipartite quantum entanglement, plays a crucial role in quantum information science due to its robust entanglement properties. Quantum uncertainty relations, on the other hand, form a fundamental cornerstone of quantum mechanics. This work introduces a…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062451] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum uncertainty relations to identify the three-qubit W state, a canonical entangled state.
motivation: The W state is important for quantum information tasks, and uncertainty relations provide a fundamental tool for characterizing quantum states.
method: The authors derive an uncertainty relation based on mutually unbiased bases and show that the W state saturates it uniquely.
result: They prove that the W state is the only three-qubit pure state achieving the minimum of the derived uncertainty relation.
conclusion: The uncertainty relation serves as a witness for the W state, offering a new method for entanglement detection.

title: Giant Magnetoelasticity In FeRh Thin Films Evidenced Via Strong Phonon-magnon Coupling
authors: D. Ourdani, C. Gourdon, J. A. Arregi, V. Uhlíř, Y. Roussigné, And L. Thevenard
abstract:
Author(s): D. Ourdani, C. Gourdon, J. A. Arregi, V. Uhlíř, Y. Roussigné, and L. Thevenard

FeRh is best known for its metamagnetic transition and giant volume magnetostriction. Here, the authors reveal remarkably strong phonon–magnon coupling in epitaxial FeRh. Combining Brillouin light scattering experiments with magnetoacoustic modeling, they demonstrate giant magnetoelasticity and show that Love surface acoustic waves provide an efficient mechanism for coherent magnon-polaron formation in magnetic thin films, highlighting FeRh as a promising platform for spin-acoustic information processing.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214450] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: FeRh thin films exhibit giant magnetoelasticity and strong phonon-magnon coupling, enabling coherent magnon-polaron formation for spin-acoustic information processing.
motivation: To explore FeRh as a platform for spin-acoustic information processing by demonstrating strong phonon-magnon coupling and giant magnetoelasticity.
method: Brillouin light scattering experiments combined with magnetoacoustic modeling to study phonon-magnon coupling in epitaxial FeRh thin films.
result: Observation of giant magnetoelasticity and strong coupling between Love surface acoustic waves and magnons, leading to coherent magnon-polaron formation.
conclusion: FeRh is a promising material for hybrid quantum systems that couple spin and acoustic degrees of freedom, relevant for quantum information processing.

title: Two-temperature Ashkin-Teller Model
authors: Sertac Cengiz And M. Cemal Yalabik
abstract:
Author(s): Sertac Cengiz and M. Cemal Yalabik

Phase diagram of the two-temperature Ashkin-Teller model with Kawasaki dynamics has been investigated. The system is placed in contact with two heat baths at different temperatures, each of which controls the dynamics of nearest-neighbor exchange in the two perpendicular directions. It was observed …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064144] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Phase diagram of the Ashkin-Teller model under two-temperature Kawasaki dynamics is studied.
motivation: To understand non-equilibrium steady states in a system coupled to two heat baths at different temperatures.
method: Monte Carlo simulations of the Ashkin-Teller model with Kawasaki dynamics, where exchange rates in perpendicular directions are controlled by separate heat baths.
result: Observed phase transitions and phase diagram features induced by the temperature difference.
conclusion: The two-temperature coupling leads to novel non-equilibrium phases not present in equilibrium.

title: Emergence Of A Luttinger Liquid Phase In An Array Of Chiral Molecules
authors: Muhammad Arsalan Ali Akbar, Bretislav Friedrich, And Sabre Kais
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Arsalan Ali Akbar, Bretislav Friedrich, and Sabre Kais

We propose a robust platform for simulating chiral quantum magnetism using linear arrays of trapped asymmetric-top molecules, specifically 1,2-propanediol ([MATH]). By mapping the Stark-dressed rotational states onto an effective spin-[MATH] subspace, we ri…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023340] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Proposes using trapped chiral molecules to simulate a Luttinger liquid phase, mapping rotational states to an effective spin-1/2 system.
motivation: To create a robust platform for simulating chiral quantum magnetism and Luttinger liquid behavior using molecular arrays.
method: Linear arrays of trapped asymmetric-top molecules (1,2-propanediol) are used, with Stark-dressed rotational states mapped onto an effective spin-1/2 subspace.
result: The system exhibits a Luttinger liquid phase with tunable interactions, demonstrating the feasibility of molecular quantum simulation.
conclusion: Trapped chiral molecules provide a viable platform for studying quantum magnetism and Luttinger liquids, with potential for further exploration of many-body physics.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics.
motivation: To provide a complete mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, bridging the gap between diffusion and jump process theories.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and continuum limits that recover diffusion results.
result: A unified stochastic calculus that treats jump and diffusion processes on equal footing, enabling consistent analysis of pathwise observables.
conclusion: The framework offers a rigorous foundation for studying stochastic thermodynamics and fluctuations in systems with both continuous and discrete dynamics.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces non-Gaussian control parameters to systematically optimize generation of non-Gaussian quantum states, improving success rates by orders of magnitude.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing but their generation is inefficient; the paper aims to provide a systematic optimization framework.
method: Defines new control parameters beyond stellar rank and uses them to design and optimize optical circuits for non-Gaussian state generation.
result: Achieves orders-of-magnitude improvement in success probability for generating target non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: The proposed control parameters enable scalable and efficient generation of non-Gaussian states, advancing optical quantum information processing.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity approaching that needed to isolate topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: Understanding entropy in strongly correlated electron systems, particularly in fractional quantum Hall states, is crucial for probing topological order and non-Abelian anyons.
method: The authors perform entropy measurements in a partially filled Landau level using a highly sensitive technique, tracking the freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom as a function of temperature and magnetic field.
result: They observe successive freezing of spin and motional entropy, achieving sensitivity that constrains the extraction of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a path toward measuring topological entropy in fractional quantum Hall systems, but the current results are more about thermodynamic characterization than direct information-theoretic or thermodynamic principles.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, enabling universal quantum computing with a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates is essential for universal quantum computing, but existing methods often require non-planar geometries or high overhead.
method: The authors design twisted color circuits that use lattice surgery and a just-in-time decoder to achieve fault tolerance for non-Clifford gates on a planar 2D color code.
result: The proposed circuits are scalable and compatible with nearest-neighbor couplings, achieving fault tolerance with reduced overhead compared to previous approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a practical pathway to universal fault-tolerant quantum computing on planar chips using color codes.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:

[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Characterizes the computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum algorithms and determining where quantum computers can outperform classical ones.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using complexity theory, likely employing reductions and oracle separations.
result: They provide a complexity classification, showing that certain regimes are classically hard but quantumly easy, while others remain hard for both.
conclusion: The work offers new insights into potential quantum advantages for matrix function computations, guiding future algorithm design.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes

abstract:

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient classical surrogate for small subregions of quantum expectation landscapes, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Classically simulating quantum circuits is hard, but for small patches of the landscape, efficient surrogates may exist, enabling hybrid quantum-classical optimization.
method: The authors develop a method to classically surrogate a subregion of an expectation landscape by leveraging initial quantum measurements and classical machine learning.
result: They show that the surrogate can be constructed efficiently and accurately for small patches, reducing quantum resource requirements.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical way to combine quantum and classical resources for variational algorithms, though limited to small subregions.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.

tldr: The paper presents symmetry-accelerated classical simulation methods for Clifford-dominated circuits using optimal stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Efficient classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verifying quantum computers, especially in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era.
method: The authors exploit strong and weak symmetry reductions to render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries, enabling faster classical simulation of circuits dominated by Clifford gates.
result: The proposed methods significantly extend the size of Clifford-dominated circuits that can be simulated classically, surpassing previous limits.
conclusion: Symmetry-accelerated stabilizer decompositions provide a practical tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, aiding in the validation of quantum devices.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited to achieve high-precision sensing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling analysis and Fisher information near critical points.
result: It demonstrates how criticality can lead to Heisenberg-limited scaling in parameter estimation.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing offers a promising route for surpassing classical limits, but practical challenges remain.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a tight-binding lattice for near-optimal quantum simulation.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints; this work aims to overcome that.
method: The authors develop a dilation approach that maps ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, using moment-matching to approximate the nonunitary evolution.
result: The method achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating linear differential equations and nonunitary dynamics.
conclusion: The framework provides an efficient way to simulate nonunitary processes on quantum hardware, with potential applications in open quantum systems and differential equation solvers.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A multiproduct commutation relation reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation by exploiting commuting structures in quantum circuits.
motivation: T-gates are costly in fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing T-count is crucial for practical quantum algorithms.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial multiproduct commutation relation that allows commuting multiple Pauli operators through T gates, enabling more efficient circuit synthesis.
result: The proposed relation significantly reduces the number of T gates required in sequential Pauli-based computation, improving overall resource efficiency.
conclusion: This work provides a new algebraic tool for T-count reduction, contributing to the optimization of fault-tolerant quantum circuits.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a rigorous definition of Majorana bound states in interacting systems to assess their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to quantify the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, using numerical simulations and analytical models.
result: They provide a framework to distinguish true Majorana bound states from trivial Andreev bound states, and quantify how interactions affect their non-Abelian properties.
conclusion: The work establishes practical metrics for identifying Majorana bound states in interacting systems, guiding future experiments on topological qubits.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a new family of quantum LDPC codes achieving single-shot error correction with improved pseudothreshold and shorter block lengths.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction typically requires multiple rounds of syndrome measurement; single-shot error correction reduces this overhead, but existing codes have large block lengths or low thresholds.
method: Constructs Abelian multi-cycle codes that are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, enabling single-shot error correction via a specific syndrome measurement schedule.
result: Achieves a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths compared to previous single-shot codes.
conclusion: The proposed codes offer a practical advantage for fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing the resource overhead of error correction.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes using code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurement is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing methods often require additional code blocks or degrade code properties.
method: The authors propose a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes while maintaining the code's distance and other properties.
result: The scheme achieves parallel measurements without extra code blocks, preserving key code properties and enabling more efficient quantum computation.
conclusion: This work advances practical fault-tolerant quantum computing by providing a resource-efficient method for parallel logical measurements.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but some measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to materials with enhanced properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of materials and phenomena where such violations occur, analyzing which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated.
result: It identifies that violations arise from non-equilibrium conditions, internal resonances, or hierarchical structures, and shows how to design materials that exploit these effects.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are not actual violations but stem from misapplied assumptions; this insight can guide the development of materials with superior properties.

title: Continuous Time Crystals As A $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$ Symmetric State And The Emergence Of Critical Exceptional Points
authors: Yuma Nakanishi, Ryo Hanai, And Tomohiro Sasamoto
abstract:
Author(s): Yuma Nakanishi, Ryo Hanai, and Tomohiro Sasamoto

Continuous time-translation symmetry is often spontaneously broken in open quantum systems, and the condition for their emergence has been actively investigated. However, there are only a few cases in which its condition for appearance has been fully elucidated. In this Letter, we show that a Lindbl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250404] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that continuous time crystals in open quantum systems can be understood as PT-symmetric states, with critical exceptional points governing their emergence.
motivation: Continuous time-translation symmetry breaking in open quantum systems is not fully understood; the authors aim to clarify the condition for its emergence using PT symmetry.
method: They analyze a Lindblad master equation and map the steady state to a PT-symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, identifying exceptional points as critical boundaries.
result: They find that the time-crystal phase corresponds to a PT-broken phase, and the transition occurs at exceptional points of the effective Hamiltonian.
conclusion: The PT-symmetric framework provides a unified condition for continuous time crystals, linking them to non-Hermitian physics and exceptional points.

title: Crystalline Spectral Form Factors
authors: Dmitrii A. Trunin And David A. Huse
abstract:
Author(s): Dmitrii A. Trunin and David A. Huse

We investigate crystallinelike behavior of the spectral form factor in unitary quantum systems with extremely strong eigenvalue repulsion. Using a low-temperature Coulomb gas as a model of repulsive eigenvalues, we derive the Debye-Waller factor suppressing periodic oscillations of the spectral form…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250405] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies crystalline spectral form factors in quantum systems with strong eigenvalue repulsion, using a Coulomb gas model to derive a Debye-Waller factor that suppresses periodic oscillations.
motivation: To understand the spectral form factor behavior in systems with extremely strong level repulsion, which is relevant to quantum chaos and random matrix theory.
method: The authors model eigenvalue repulsion using a low-temperature Coulomb gas and compute the spectral form factor analytically, identifying a Debye-Waller factor that suppresses oscillations.
result: They find that the spectral form factor exhibits a crystalline behavior with suppressed oscillations, analogous to the Debye-Waller effect in solids.
conclusion: The work provides a new perspective on spectral statistics in strongly repulsive systems, linking quantum chaos to crystallinelike order.

title: Protection Of Quantum Steering Ellipsoids In non-Markovian Environments
authors: Wen-Jie Zhang And Jun-Hong An
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Jie Zhang and Jun-Hong An

Quantum steering ellipsoids (QSEs) provide a geometric representation, within the Bloch picture, of all possible states to which one qubit can be steered through measuring another correlated qubit. However, in realistic settings, quantum systems are inevitably coupled to their environment, resulting…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062458] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the protection of quantum steering ellipsoids from decoherence using non-Markovian environments.
motivation: Quantum steering ellipsoids provide a geometric representation of steerable states, but decoherence degrades them; understanding protection mechanisms is important for quantum information tasks.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of quantum steering ellipsoids under non-Markovian noise, using master equations and geometric measures.
result: Non-Markovian environments can preserve the volume and shape of steering ellipsoids better than Markovian ones, depending on the noise parameters.
conclusion: Non-Markovian effects can be harnessed to protect quantum steering correlations, which may benefit quantum communication protocols.

title: Higher-order Liouvillian Exceptional Points In The Dissipative Dynamics Of Quadratic Fermions
authors: Mingtao Xu And Wei Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Mingtao Xu and Wei Yi

We propose a general class of open fermionic models where quadratic Liouvillians governing the dissipative dynamics feature analytically characterized higher-order exceptional points (EPs). Invoking the formalism of third quantization, we show that, among the multiple EPs of Liouvillian, an EP with …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062455] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies higher-order exceptional points in the dissipative dynamics of quadratic fermions, focusing on Liouvillian spectral properties.
motivation: Exceptional points in open quantum systems are of interest for their unique spectral degeneracies, but higher-order Liouvillian EPs in fermionic systems are not well understood.
method: Using third quantization formalism, the authors analytically characterize higher-order EPs in quadratic Liouvillians and study their signatures in dynamics.
result: They identify multiple EPs and show that an EP with the highest order governs the asymptotic dynamics, with observable effects in fermionic parity and correlation functions.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for understanding higher-order EPs in dissipative fermionic systems, but the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Proposals For Realizing A Josephson Diode In Atomtronic Circuits
authors: Nalinikanta Pradhan, Rina Kanamoto, M. Bhattacharya, And Pankaj Kumar Mishra
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061502] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a Josephson diode in atomtronic circuits using asymmetric junction placement and driving to achieve nonreciprocal transport.
motivation: To realize a highly controllable neutral-atom platform for quantum circuitry and atomtronic devices.
method: Theoretical proposal using a ring condensate with asymmetric junction placement and driving to break symmetry and induce nonreciprocal Josephson transport.
result: Achieves Josephson diode effect with efficiencies up to 91%.
conclusion: The atomtronic platform offers a controllable neutral-atom system for future quantum circuitry.

title: Hexapartite Active Nonlinear Feedback Control In Four-wave Mixing With A Spatially Structured Pump
authors: Guanjun Zeng, Xiaozhou Pan, Kai Zhang, And Jietai Jing
abstract:

In the field of quantum information science, feedback control has become an important method for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams. Here we theoretically propose an active nonlinear feedback control system utilizing two four-wave-mixing processes [MATH] and [MATH]…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062448] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an active nonlinear feedback control system using two four-wave-mixing processes with a spatially structured pump for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams.
motivation: Feedback control is important for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams in quantum information science.
method: The authors theoretically design a system with two four-wave-mixing processes and a spatially structured pump to achieve active nonlinear feedback control.
result: The system enables control over nonclassical beams, though specific performance metrics are not detailed in the abstract.
conclusion: The proposed feedback control scheme may be useful for quantum information applications, but the paper is theoretical and lacks experimental validation.

title: Apparent Bistability From Weak Long-range Interactions
authors: Achilleas Lazarides And Andrea Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Achilleas Lazarides and Andrea Pizzi

Bistability, or the coexistence of two stable phases, can be broken by a bias field [MATH] destabilizing one of the phases via the nucleation and growth of defects. Strong long-range interactions, [MATH] with [MATH] less than the system's dimensionality [MATH], can suppress the proliferation of defects …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224116] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies apparent bistability in systems with weak long-range interactions, showing that such interactions can suppress defect nucleation and lead to metastable phases.
motivation: Understanding how long-range interactions affect phase coexistence and metastability is important for non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze a classical or quantum model with weak long-range interactions, likely using mean-field theory or numerical simulations to study defect dynamics and phase stability.
result: Weak long-range interactions can stabilize apparent bistability by suppressing the nucleation and growth of defects that would otherwise destroy one phase.
conclusion: The findings highlight the role of interaction range in determining phase behavior, with implications for systems where long-range forces are present.

title: Anisotropic Second-harmonic Generation In Superconducting Nanostructures
authors: Sara Memarzadeh, Maciej Krawczyk, Armen Gulian, And Jarosław W. Kłos
abstract:

Circuits based on superconducting nanostructures are among the most promising platforms for quantum computing. Understanding how device geometry governs nonlinear electrodynamics is crucial for implementing superconducting quantum technologies. However, to date, research has largely been limited to …
