tldr: This paper studies anisotropic second-harmonic generation in superconducting nanostructures, focusing on geometry-dependent nonlinear electrodynamics.
motivation: Understanding how device geometry governs nonlinear electrodynamics is crucial for implementing superconducting quantum technologies.
method: The authors theoretically analyze second-harmonic generation in superconducting nanostructures with different geometries, likely using nonlinear response theory or numerical simulations.
result: They find that the second-harmonic response is anisotropic and strongly dependent on the nanostructure geometry.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonlinear effects in superconducting circuits, which may inform design of quantum devices but does not directly address quantum information processing or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Anomalous Quantum Relaxation In The Infinite-temperature Hubbard Chain
authors: Cătălin Paşcu Moca And Balázs Dóra
abstract:
Author(s): Cătălin Paşcu Moca and Balázs Dóra

The self-energy encodes the fundamental lifetime of quasiparticle excitations. In one dimension, it is known to display anomalous behavior at zero temperature for interacting fermions, reflecting the breakdown of Fermi-liquid theory. Here we show that the self-energy is also anomalous in the infinit…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241120] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that the self-energy in the infinite-temperature Hubbard chain exhibits anomalous relaxation, indicating non-Fermi-liquid behavior even at high temperatures.
motivation: Understanding quasiparticle lifetimes in one-dimensional systems is fundamental, and anomalous self-energy at zero temperature is known; this work extends the study to infinite temperature.
method: The authors compute the self-energy analytically and numerically for the Hubbard chain at infinite temperature using Bethe ansatz and other techniques.
result: They find that the self-energy decays as a power law in frequency, with an exponent that depends on interaction strength, signaling anomalous relaxation.
conclusion: The anomalous behavior persists at infinite temperature, suggesting that non-Fermi-liquid physics is not limited to low temperatures in 1D.

title: Signatures Of Quantum Chaos And Complexity In The Ising Model On Random Graphs
authors: G. J. Sreejith And Sandipan Manna
abstract:
Author(s): G. J. Sreejith and Sandipan Manna

We investigate signatures of quantum chaos in the mixed-field quantum Ising model on finite-size Erdős–Rényi graphs using probes scalable on near-term quantum devices. Upon tuning the graph connectivity, the system exhibits a crossover from a localized regime at low connectivity, through a chaotic r…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214322] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies quantum chaos and complexity in the Ising model on random graphs using probes scalable on near-term quantum devices.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos in many-body systems is important for characterizing thermalization and complexity, but the paper focuses on a specific model (Ising on random graphs) without direct connection to thermodynamics or information theory.
method: The authors use spectral statistics (level spacing ratios) and out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) to probe chaos in the mixed-field quantum Ising model on Erdős–Rényi graphs with varying connectivity.
result: They observe a crossover from localized to chaotic regimes as connectivity increases, and identify signatures of quantum chaos that are accessible on near-term quantum devices.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum chaos in disordered systems, but does not address thermodynamic constraints, information processing, or quantum speed limits.

title: Universality Of Dissipative Discrete Time Crystal Formation
authors: Jr. And Jayson G. Cosme Roy D. Jara
abstract:
Author(s): Roy D. Jara, Jr. and Jayson G. Cosme

We demonstrate that the Kibble-Zurek mechanism holds for open systems transitioning from a disordered phase to a discrete time crystal (DTC). Specifically, we observe the characteristic power-law scaling with quench time of the number of spatial defects and the transition delay measured from the tim…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214323] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that the Kibble-Zurek mechanism applies to open systems transitioning to a discrete time crystal phase.
motivation: To understand universal scaling behavior in dissipative phase transitions to discrete time crystals.
method: Numerical simulations of an open quantum system model, analyzing defect density and transition delay as functions of quench time.
result: Observed power-law scaling of spatial defects and transition delay with quench time, consistent with the Kibble-Zurek mechanism.
conclusion: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism is universal for dissipative discrete time crystal formation, extending its applicability to open systems.

title: Scaling And Universality At Noise-affected Nonequilibrium Spin Correlation Functions
authors: R. Jafari And Alireza Akbari
abstract:
Author(s): R. Jafari and Alireza Akbari

We investigate the scaling and universality of the asymptotic behavior of nonequilibrium spin correlation functions in the presence of uncorrelated noise. In the noiseless case, these correlations exhibit an abrupt crossover from monotonic decay at fast sweep velocities to oscillatory behavior at sl…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220302] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies scaling and universality in nonequilibrium spin correlation functions under noise, focusing on a crossover from monotonic to oscillatory decay.
motivation: Understanding how noise affects nonequilibrium dynamics and universality in quantum many-body systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and control.
method: The authors analyze spin correlation functions in the presence of uncorrelated noise using analytical and numerical methods, examining scaling behavior.
result: They find that noise modifies the crossover between monotonic and oscillatory decay, and identify universal scaling exponents.
conclusion: The results provide insight into noise-induced changes in nonequilibrium quantum dynamics, relevant for quantum thermal machines and information processing.

title: Nonuniversal Thermal Hall Responses In Fractional Quantum Hall Droplets
authors: Fei Tan, Yuzhu Wang, Xinghao Wang, And Bo Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Fei Tan, Yuzhu Wang, Xinghao Wang, and Bo Yang

We analytically compute the thermal Hall conductance (THC) of fractional quantum Hall droplets under realistic conditions that go beyond the idealized linear edge theory with conformal symmetry. Specifically, we consider finite-size effects at low temperature, nonzero self-energies of quasiholes, an…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241118] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper computes thermal Hall conductance of fractional quantum Hall droplets beyond idealized edge theory, considering finite-size and self-energy effects.
motivation: To understand thermal Hall responses in realistic fractional quantum Hall systems, which are relevant for topological order and potential quantum information applications.
method: Analytical computation of thermal Hall conductance using edge theory with corrections from finite-size effects and quasihole self-energies.
result: The thermal Hall conductance deviates from universal quantized values due to nonuniversal corrections at low temperatures and finite sizes.
conclusion: Realistic fractional quantum Hall droplets exhibit nonuniversal thermal Hall responses, which must be accounted for in experiments and potential topological quantum computing applications.

title: Magnetoelastic Signatures Of Thermal And Quantum Phase Transitions In A Deformable Ising Chain Under A Longitudinal And Transverse Magnetic Field
authors: Dávid Sivý And Jozef Strečka
abstract:
Author(s): Dávid Sivý and Jozef Strečka

We investigate a deformable spin-1/2 Ising chain subjected to either a longitudinal or a transverse magnetic field, which incorporates a magnetoelastic coupling linearly dependent on a lattice distortion parameter. Within the harmonic and static adiabatic approximations, the variational Gibbs free e…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064146] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies magnetoelastic signatures of thermal and quantum phase transitions in a deformable Ising chain under magnetic fields.
motivation: To understand how magnetoelastic coupling affects phase transitions in low-dimensional spin systems.
method: Variational Gibbs free energy approach within harmonic and static adiabatic approximations for a spin-1/2 Ising chain with magnetoelastic coupling.
result: Identifies magnetoelastic signatures that distinguish thermal and quantum phase transitions.
conclusion: Magnetoelastic coupling provides a sensitive probe of phase transitions in deformable spin chains.

title: Vanishing Correlations In Stochastic And Bistochastic Controlled Circuits
authors: Pavel Kos, Bruno Bertini, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Pavel Kos, Bruno Bertini, and Tomaž Prosen

We study the dynamics of circuits composed of stochastic and bistochastic controlled gates. This type of dynamics arises from quantum circuits with random controlled gates, as well as in stochastic circuits and deterministic classical cellular automata. We prove that stochastic and bistochastic cont…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064139] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that correlations vanish in stochastic and bistochastic controlled circuits, with implications for quantum circuits and classical cellular automata.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of random quantum circuits and their classical counterparts is important for quantum information and statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze circuits composed of stochastic and bistochastic controlled gates using mathematical proofs and possibly numerical simulations.
result: They show that under certain conditions, correlations decay to zero, indicating a loss of quantum or classical correlations.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the behavior of random circuits and may inform the design of quantum algorithms or error correction.

title: Intrinsic Nonreciprocity In Electron-phonon-interaction-driven Thermoelectric Diodes
authors: Hao-Kun Ke, Lie-Run Tian, Jun-Feng Liu, Pei-Hao Fu, Jun Wang, And Hu Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Hao-Kun Ke, Lie-Run Tian, Jun-Feng Liu, Pei-Hao Fu, Jun Wang, and Hu Xu

Researchers demonstrate intrinsic nonreciprocal thermoelectric transport in electron-phonon coupled nanowire devices, arising from asymmetric phonon emission and absorption and structural asymmetry. The intrinsic nonreciprocity results in a load-resistor resistance reduction effect that violates Ohm’s addition law in the incoherent limit.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022058] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates intrinsic nonreciprocal thermoelectric transport in electron-phonon coupled nanowire devices, leading to a violation of Ohm's addition law.
motivation: To explore nonreciprocal transport in thermoelectric systems driven by electron-phonon interactions, which could enable novel diode-like behavior.
method: The authors study a nanowire device with structural asymmetry and electron-phonon coupling, analyzing phonon emission and absorption asymmetries to derive nonreciprocal transport coefficients.
result: They find that the intrinsic nonreciprocity causes a load-resistor resistance reduction effect that violates Ohm's addition law in the incoherent limit.
conclusion: The work reveals a fundamental mechanism for nonreciprocal thermoelectric transport, with potential applications in energy conversion and thermal management.

title: Tunable Intertwining Via Collective Excitations
authors: András Szabó And R. Chitra
abstract:
Author(s): András Szabó and R. Chitra

Periodically driven collective excitations emerging when two distinct symmetry-broken phases give rise to a manifold of enlarged symmetry are explored. The work proposes that the resulting driven phase diagram hosting out-of-equilibrium intertwined phases is accessible in state-of-the-art matter-cavity experimental setups.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022053] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies periodically driven collective excitations in symmetry-broken phases, proposing a tunable intertwined phase accessible in matter-cavity setups.
motivation: To explore out-of-equilibrium phases arising from driving collective excitations in systems with enlarged symmetry manifolds.
method: Theoretical analysis of periodically driven symmetry-broken phases, deriving the driven phase diagram.
result: A tunable intertwined phase is predicted, accessible in state-of-the-art matter-cavity experiments.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for engineering out-of-equilibrium intertwined phases via periodic driving.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally expensive; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to accelerate simulations.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables in frequency space, capturing temporal correlations.
result: The method accurately predicts Floquet Hamiltonians, observable dynamics, and operator growth beyond the training time window.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and extrapolative tool for simulating time-periodic quantum systems.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols classically is often computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: The method involves propagating errors through the circuit to the end, allowing for a simplified simulation that avoids tracking all intermediate error correlations.
result: The approach achieves polynomial-time simulation for a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols, significantly reducing computational cost.
conclusion: This work enables practical classical simulation of magic state preparation, which is important for verifying and optimizing fault-tolerant quantum computing protocols.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying diverse approaches for modeling complex systems.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but existing methods are fragmented; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors review field-theoretic techniques (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review shows how field theories provide a systematic way to compute correlation functions and effective dynamics for these systems.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying approach for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across disciplines.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems for novel material properties.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory and pump-probe spectroscopy.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable phases, and nonthermal orders like superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation in Mott insulators enables rich nonequilibrium phenomena with potential for ultrafast control of material properties.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the complexity-theoretic foundations of BosonSampling to the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, proving hardness for approximate sampling.
motivation: Previous BosonSampling complexity proofs assumed a dilute regime (many more modes than photons), but experimental demonstrations operate in a saturated regime with comparable numbers of modes and photons. The gap needed to be bridged to justify quantum advantage claims.
method: The authors develop new anticoncentration bounds and use random matrix theory to show that the output distribution of linear-optical circuits in the saturated regime is sufficiently complex to be hard to sample classically, assuming standard conjectures.
result: They prove that approximate BosonSampling with a linear number of modes is #P-hard under plausible complexity assumptions, and provide evidence that the distribution is anticoncentrated.
conclusion: The results validate that current photonic quantum advantage experiments in the saturated regime are on solid complexity-theoretic ground, reinforcing the case for quantum supremacy in photonics.

title: Ferromagnetism Versus Antiferromagnetism In Narrow-Band Systems: Competition Between Quantum Geometry And Band Dispersion
authors: Haoyu Hu, Oskar Vafek, Kristjan Haule, And B. Andrei Bernevig
abstract:
Author(s): Haoyu Hu, Oskar Vafek, Kristjan Haule, and B. Andrei Bernevig

Magnetism in narrow-band systems arises from the interplay between electronic correlations, quantum geometry, and band dispersion. In particular, both ferro and antiferro magnets are known to occur as ground states of (different) models featuring narrow bands. This poses the question of which is fav…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256505] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the competition between ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism in narrow-band systems, focusing on the role of quantum geometry and band dispersion.
motivation: Understanding the origin of magnetic order in narrow-band systems is important for correlated electron physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical models and possibly numerical methods to analyze the interplay of correlations, quantum geometry, and band dispersion.
result: They identify conditions under which ferromagnetic or antiferromagnetic order is favored.
conclusion: Quantum geometry plays a key role in determining magnetic ground states in narrow-band systems.

title: Pseudo-Hermitian Symmetry Breaking And Re-entrant Localization In A One-dimensional non-Hermitian Chain
authors: Pei-Lin Wang, Ai-Bo Xia, Jun-Bo Zhao, Hong-Tao Fan, And Y. P. Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Pei-Lin Wang, Ai-Bo Xia, Jun-Bo Zhao, Hong-Tao Fan, and Y. P. Wang

Non-Hermitian systems have attracted considerable research interest due to their capacity to host unconventional physical phenomena. However, research on pseudo-Hermitian symmetry and re-entrant localization in one-dimensional non-Hermitian settings remain relatively limited. Here, we propose a one-…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063736] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies pseudo-Hermitian symmetry breaking and re-entrant localization in a one-dimensional non-Hermitian chain.
motivation: Non-Hermitian systems exhibit unconventional phenomena, but pseudo-Hermitian symmetry and re-entrant localization in 1D are underexplored.
method: The authors propose a 1D non-Hermitian chain model and analyze its spectral and localization properties using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They observe pseudo-Hermitian symmetry breaking and re-entrant localization transitions as parameters vary.
conclusion: The work extends understanding of non-Hermitian physics, particularly symmetry and localization, in one-dimensional systems.

title: Flat-band Driven Kondo Breakdown And Reentrant Effects In Heavy-fermion Moiré Superlattices
authors: Fabian Eickhoff, Jian-Xin Zhu, And Benedikt Fauseweh
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Eickhoff, Jian-Xin Zhu, and Benedikt Fauseweh

Moiré superlattices (MSLs) in van der Waals heterostructures have demonstrated their incredible power in driving emergent electronic phenomena, some of which are reminiscent of those usually only observed in bulk strongly correlated quantum materials. With the recent discovery of van der Waals [MATH]-e…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235153] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kondo breakdown and reentrant effects in heavy-fermion moiré superlattices, focusing on flat-band driven electronic phenomena.
motivation: Moiré superlattices in van der Waals heterostructures can host emergent strongly correlated electronic phases, and understanding Kondo physics in these systems may reveal new quantum states.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and numerical methods to analyze the Kondo lattice model in a moiré superlattice with flat bands.
result: They find that flat bands can drive a Kondo breakdown transition and lead to reentrant heavy-fermion behavior as a function of doping or temperature.
conclusion: The work highlights the rich interplay between flat-band geometry and strong correlations in moiré systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Orbital Magnetization Reveals Multiband Topology
authors: Chun Wang Chau, Robert-Jan Slager, And Wojciech J. Jankowski
abstract:
Author(s): Chun Wang Chau, Robert-Jan Slager, and Wojciech J. Jankowski

We demonstrate that nontrivial multiband topological invariants of electronic wave functions can be revealed through orbital magnetization responses to external magnetic fields. We find that decomposing orbital magnetization into energetic and quantum-geometric contributions allows one to deduce non…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235154] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that orbital magnetization can reveal multiband topological invariants in electronic systems.
motivation: To find a physical observable that directly probes multiband topology beyond the usual single-band Chern number.
method: Decompose orbital magnetization into energetic and quantum-geometric contributions and relate them to topological invariants.
result: The decomposition allows extraction of multiband topological invariants from magnetization responses.
conclusion: Orbital magnetization is a useful probe for multiband topology, offering a new experimental signature.

title: Tracking Doublon-holon Dynamics In High-harmonic Generation From Mott Insulators
authors: Tao-Yuan Du, Hui-Ru Li, Bo Li, And Ruifeng Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Tao-Yuan Du, Hui-Ru Li, Bo Li, and Ruifeng Lu

High-harmonic generation (HHG) in strongly correlated Mott insulators is investigated using exact diagonalization and time-dependent density-matrix propagation of a laser-driven one-dimensional Hubbard chain. By projecting onto equilibrium Hubbard bands, we use the doublon population and its dynamic…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245147] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies high-harmonic generation in Mott insulators using exact diagonalization and time-dependent density-matrix propagation.
motivation: To understand the microscopic dynamics of doublon-holon pairs in strongly correlated systems under strong laser fields.
method: Exact diagonalization and time-dependent density-matrix propagation of a laser-driven one-dimensional Hubbard chain.
result: The doublon population dynamics are linked to high-harmonic generation spectra.
conclusion: The work provides insight into non-equilibrium dynamics in Mott insulators but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Exceptional Rings Emerging In A non-Hermitian Rice-Mele Ladder
authors: Ensuo Ma And Zhi Song
abstract:
Author(s): Ensuo Ma and Zhi Song

Weyl exceptional lines typically occur in three-dimensional (3D) topological semimetals; however, they also emerge in the parameter space of one-dimensional (1D) systems. In this work, we study the impact of dissipation on the nodal ring in a 3D topological semimetal. We find that the energy spectru…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235150] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exceptional rings in a non-Hermitian Rice-Mele ladder, focusing on topological semimetal physics with dissipation.
motivation: To understand the impact of dissipation on nodal rings in 3D topological semimetals, using a 1D ladder model as a parameter space analog.
method: The authors analyze a non-Hermitian Rice-Mele ladder model, deriving the energy spectrum and identifying exceptional rings in parameter space.
result: Exceptional rings emerge in the parameter space of the 1D ladder, analogous to Weyl exceptional lines in 3D semimetals.
conclusion: The work extends the concept of exceptional lines to lower-dimensional systems, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Model With Competing Rashba Spin-orbit Interactions, Higher Order Hopping, And Domain Wall
authors: Hemant Kumar Sharma, Arijit Saha, And Saptarshi Mandal
abstract:
Author(s): Hemant Kumar Sharma, Arijit Saha, and Saptarshi Mandal

We investigate an extended spin-full Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model preserving chiral symmetry. It contains spin-mixing and nonmixing Rashba spin-orbit interactions, complex next to next nearest neighbor (NNNN) hopping. Using the theory of non-Hermitian matrices, we construct a Hamiltonian functio…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245143] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies an extended SSH model with Rashba spin-orbit interactions and higher-order hopping, focusing on topological phases and domain walls.
motivation: To understand the interplay of spin-orbit coupling and long-range hopping in topological insulators.
method: Constructs a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian and analyzes topological invariants and edge states.
result: Finds that Rashba interactions and NNNN hopping modify the topological phase diagram and domain wall states.
conclusion: The extended SSH model exhibits rich topological behavior, but the work is primarily condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Controlled Pairing Symmetries In A Fermi-Hubbard Ladder With Band Flattening
authors: João P. Mendonça, S. Biswas, M. Dziurawiec, U. Bhattacharya, K. Jachymski, M. Aidelsburger, M. Lewenstein, M. M. Maśka, And T. Grass
abstract:
Author(s): João P. Mendonça, S. Biswas, M. Dziurawiec, U. Bhattacharya, K. Jachymski, M. Aidelsburger, M. Lewenstein, M. M. Maśka, and T. Grass

The competition between interactions in systems with slow electrons can drive unusual collective behavior. Here, the authors study a microscopic ladder model featuring both diagonal hopping pathways and complex loop-like electron exchange interactions. They demonstrate that while both mechanisms independently suppress ordinary metallic behavior, they stabilize completely distinct spatial patterns of electron pairing. These findings offer a theoretical framework for engineering specific superconducting states by tuning the competition between pairing mechanisms in platforms like twisted bilayer graphene or cold atoms.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241119] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies controlled pairing symmetries in a Fermi-Hubbard ladder with band flattening, focusing on competing pairing mechanisms and their spatial patterns.
motivation: To understand how slow electrons and competing interactions can stabilize distinct superconducting states in systems like twisted bilayer graphene or cold atoms.
method: The authors analyze a microscopic ladder model with diagonal hopping and complex loop-like exchange interactions, using theoretical and numerical methods to study the resulting pairing symmetries.
result: They find that diagonal hopping and loop exchange independently suppress metallic behavior but stabilize completely different spatial patterns of electron pairing.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for engineering specific superconducting states by tuning the competition between pairing mechanisms.

title: Differentiable Learning And Control Of Free-energy-driven Pattern Dynamics
authors: Alexander E. Cohen, Samuel Degnan-Morgenstern, Simon Daubner, Jörn Dunkel, And Martin Z. Bazant
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander E. Cohen, Samuel Degnan-Morgenstern, Simon Daubner, Jörn Dunkel, and Martin Z. Bazant

Pattern-forming dynamics govern the behavior of many quantum, electrochemical, and soft-matter systems, yet learning and controlling the corresponding partial differential equation (PDE) models on realistic geometries remains challenging. In this work, we develop a unified, differentiable framework …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023344] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A differentiable framework for learning and controlling pattern-forming PDEs in soft-matter and electrochemical systems.
motivation: Pattern-forming dynamics are important in many physical systems, but learning and controlling PDE models on realistic geometries is challenging.
method: Develops a unified differentiable framework combining neural networks and adjoint methods to learn and control free-energy-driven pattern dynamics.
result: Demonstrates effective learning and control of pattern formation in several examples, including electrochemical and soft-matter systems.
conclusion: The framework enables data-driven discovery and control of pattern-forming PDEs, with potential applications in materials science and engineering.

title: Simulating Dynamics Of The Two-dimensional Transverse-field Ising Model: A Comparative Study Of Large-scale Classical Numerics
authors: Joseph Vovrosh, Sergi Julià-Farré, Wladislaw Krinitsin, Michael Kaicher, Fergus Hayes, Emmanuel Gottlob, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Kemal Bidzhiev, Simon B. Jäger, Markus Schmitt, Joseph Tindall, Constantin Dalyac, Tiago Mendes-Santos, And Alexandre Dauphin
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph Vovrosh, Sergi Julià-Farré, Wladislaw Krinitsin, Michael Kaicher, Fergus Hayes, Emmanuel Gottlob, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Kemal Bidzhiev, Simon B. Jäger, Markus Schmitt, Joseph Tindall, Constantin Dalyac, Tiago Mendes-Santos, and Alexandre Dauphin

The quantum dynamics of many-qubit systems is an outstanding problem that has recently driven significant advances in both numerical methods and programmable quantum processing units (QPUs). In this work, we employ a comprehensive toolbox of state-of-the-art numerical approaches to classically simul…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023311] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks classical numerical methods for simulating the 2D transverse-field Ising model dynamics.
motivation: Quantum dynamics of many-qubit systems is computationally hard; this work compares various classical numerical approaches to assess their accuracy and efficiency.
method: Applies a suite of state-of-the-art numerical methods (e.g., tensor networks, neural quantum states, exact diagonalization) to simulate the 2D transverse-field Ising model.
result: Provides a comparative analysis of the performance and limitations of each method for different parameter regimes.
conclusion: No single method is universally optimal; the choice depends on the specific regime and desired accuracy.

title: Disorder-induced Topological Phases In A Two-dimensional Chern Insulator With Strong Magnetic Disorder
authors: Devesh Vaish And Michael Potthoff
abstract:
Author(s): Devesh Vaish and Michael Potthoff

Strong directional disorder in local magnetic moments coupled to a Chern insulator gives rise to topological phases that cannot be realized in any clean system and are therefore genuinely disorder driven. We demonstrate this in a spinful Qi-Wu-Zhang model of a two-dimensional Chern insulator coupled…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023312] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies disorder-induced topological phases in a Chern insulator with strong magnetic disorder, demonstrating that disorder can drive topological phases not present in clean systems.
motivation: To explore whether strong directional disorder in local magnetic moments can induce new topological phases in a two-dimensional Chern insulator, beyond those achievable in clean systems.
method: The authors consider a spinful Qi-Wu-Zhang model of a Chern insulator coupled to local magnetic moments with strong directional disorder, and analyze the resulting topological phases using numerical methods.
result: They find that strong disorder gives rise to topological phases that are genuinely disorder-driven and cannot be realized in any clean system.
conclusion: Disorder can be a resource for engineering novel topological phases in Chern insulators, expanding the possibilities for topological matter.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan

conclusion: The ultracold-atom platform can serve as a viable quantum simulator for demonstrating quantum advantage in many-body physics.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models

result: They find that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, leading to a breakdown of the thermodynamic limit.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified framework.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of the space-time duality approach and its relationship to quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality provides a powerful tool for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum circuits.

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256605] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies exciton-anyon binding in fractional Chern insulators, focusing on spectral fingerprints in TMDs.
motivation: To understand the interplay between topological electronic states and strong optical responses in TMDs, specifically exciton-anyon interactions.
method: The authors model an interacting fermion-boson system coupling excitons to anyonic quasiparticles in fractional Chern insulators and compute spectral properties.
result: They identify spectral signatures of exciton-anyon binding, such as shifts and broadening in optical spectra.
conclusion: Exciton-anyon binding provides a way to probe anyonic statistics optically in fractional Chern insulators.

authors: G. Theodorou And S. Komineas

tldr: The paper studies antiferromagnetic domain wall dynamics under spin-orbit torque, a topic in condensed matter physics with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding domain wall motion in antiferromagnets is important for spintronic devices, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors theoretically analyze domain wall profiles and dynamics using micromagnetic modeling and spin-orbit torque effects.

conclusion: The dynamics are tunable by current polarization, offering potential for spintronic applications.

tldr: This paper revisits the charge-density-wave superlattice in 1T-TiSe2, focusing on structural and electronic properties without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To resolve controversies about the CDW structure in 1T-TiSe2, which is important for understanding exciton condensation and chirality.
method: Combines electron diffraction, scanning tunneling microscopy, and first-principles calculations to determine the atomic-scale CDW superlattice.
result: Identifies a specific CDW superlattice pattern and clarifies the role of orbital ordering.
conclusion: Provides a definitive structural model for the CDW phase, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Curvature-Induced Magnon Frequency Combs
authors: Hao Zhao, Qianjun Zheng, And Peng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Zhao, Qianjun Zheng, and Peng Yan

A tiny bump in a magnetic film exposed to microwaves can engender spin waves with precisely spaced frequencies.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256708] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A bump in a magnetic film generates magnon frequency combs under microwave driving.
motivation: To explore nonlinear spin-wave dynamics and generate frequency combs in magnetic systems.
method: Theoretical analysis of curvature-induced magnon interactions in a magnetic film with a bump.
result: Precisely spaced magnon frequencies are produced, forming a frequency comb.
conclusion: Curvature in magnetic films can be used to engineer magnon frequency combs for potential applications.

title: Antiferroaxial Altermagnetism

tldr: The paper introduces antiferroaxial altermagnetism as a multiferroic mechanism combining antiferroaxial distortions and altermagnetism.
motivation: To establish a new multiferroic mechanism that couples antiferroaxial order with altermagnetism, which may have implications for spintronics and multiferroics.
method: The authors use symmetry analysis and first-principles calculations to demonstrate the prevalence of antiferroaxial altermagnetism in various materials.

conclusion: Antiferroaxial altermagnetism is a generic and microscopically grounded multiferroic mechanism with potential for novel functionalities.

title: Enhancing Hot-Carrier Lifetime Through Spin Splitting And Strain Interaction In Chiral Perovskite Materials
authors: Yuling Huang, Xiao-Feng Luo, Shaokuan Gong, Jie Xue, Haipeng Lu, Jin-Zhu Zhao, And Xihan Chen

tldr: This paper demonstrates all-optical control of spin splitting and hot-carrier lifetime enhancement in chiral 2D perovskites via strain interaction.
motivation: To achieve dynamical control over electronic properties in condensed-matter systems, specifically enhancing hot-carrier lifetimes for potential optoelectronic applications.
method: Ultrafast circular dichroism measurements and theoretical modeling to study carrier-strain-mediated spin splitting in chiral 2D perovskite materials.
result: Giant enhancement of spin splitting (100 meV) and increased hot-carrier lifetime through all-optical control of strain.
conclusion: The interaction between spin splitting and strain in chiral perovskites offers a pathway to control carrier dynamics, relevant for optoelectronics but not directly tied to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Trion Formation And Ordering In The Attractive Su(3) Fermi-Hubbard Model
authors: Jonathan Stepp, Eduardo Ibarra-García-Padilla, Richard T. Scalettar, And Kaden R. A. Hazzard

tldr: The paper proposes a nonperturbative renormalization group flow equation for generating S-matrix elements, drawing analogies to Wetterich and Polchinski equations.
motivation: To develop a renormalization group approach directly for on-shell S-matrix elements, bypassing off-shell effective actions.
method: The authors derive a functional flow equation for an S-matrix generating functional, using techniques similar to functional renormalization group methods.
result: They obtain a nonperturbative equation that captures the renormalization of scattering amplitudes without relying on off-shell quantities.
conclusion: This approach provides a new tool for studying nonperturbative aspects of quantum field theories directly from S-matrix elements.

result: A linear scaling between Tc and the angle of crystal orientation is observed.
conclusion: The linear scaling suggests a simple geometric origin for the orientation dependence, but the underlying mechanism remains to be explained.

The frequency structure of the superconducting correlations in cuprates gives insights on the pairing mechanism. title: Ultrafast Magneto-Optical Fingerprints Of Altermagnetism In MnTe

Recently identified altermagnets exhibit a distinctive dual-space nature: they possess spin-split electronic bands akin to ferromagnets in momentum space while maintaining the fully compensated magnetization of antiferromagnets in real space. result: The parametrization covers the entire state space of structured light modes except for isolated coordinate singularities.

title: Quantum Image Encodings For Noisy Intermediate-scale Quantum Devices: A Comprehensive Performance And Noise-resilience Analysis
authors: Emmanuel Martínez-Guerrero, Guo-Hua Sun, And Shi-Hai Dong

conclusion: The choice of encoding must balance expressiveness and noise tolerance for practical NISQ applications.

title: Optimal Displacement Detection Of Arbitrarily Shaped Levitated Dielectric Objects Using Optical Radiation
authors: Shaun Laing, Shelby Klomp, George Winstone, Alexey Grinin, Andrew Dana, Zhiyuan Wang, Kevin Seca Widyatmodjo, James Bateman, And Andrew A. Geraci

title: Phase-space Open-system Dynamics Of Second-order Nonlinear Interactions With Pulsed Quantum Light

motivation: Isotope shift due to alkali polarization field is a major systematic error in comagnetometer studies, limiting precision.
method: The authors model the spin-exchange collisions between Xe and alkali-metal atoms and derive the effect of inhomogeneous polarization on the measured signal.
result: They quantify how inhomogeneous alkali-spin polarization leads to systematic errors in gyroscope and comagnetometer readings.
conclusion: Understanding and mitigating these errors is crucial for improving the accuracy of NMR gyroscopes and comagnetometers.

title: Structures And Proximity Effects Of Inhomogeneous Population-imbalanced Fermi Gases With Pairing Interactions
authors: Bishal Parajuli, Devin J. Gagnon, And Chih-Chun Chien
abstract:
Author(s): Bishal Parajuli, Devin J. Gagnon, and Chih-Chun Chien

By introducing spatially varying profiles of pairing interaction or spin polarization to quasi-one-dimensional two-component atomic Fermi gases confined in box potentials, we analyze the ground-state structures and properties when multiple phases coexist in real space by implementing the Bogoliubov–…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063324] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ground-state structures of inhomogeneous population-imbalanced Fermi gases with pairing interactions using Bogoliubov–de Gennes theory.
motivation: To understand how spatially varying pairing interactions or spin polarization affect phase coexistence in quasi-one-dimensional Fermi gases.
method: The authors implement Bogoliubov–de Gennes theory to analyze ground-state structures of two-component atomic Fermi gases in box potentials with spatially varying profiles.
result: They identify multiple coexisting phases in real space and characterize their properties.
conclusion: The work provides insights into inhomogeneous Fermi gases but is focused on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Atom-chip Interferometer
authors: B. Wirtschafter, C. I. Westbrook, And M. Dupont-Nivet
abstract:
Author(s): B. Wirtschafter, C. I. Westbrook, and M. Dupont-Nivet

We have realized an interferometer using a thermal cloud of magnetically trapped rubidium-87 atoms on a chip. The interferometer resembles a Ramsey interferometer with a state selective spatial splitting of the two internal states as proposed by [M. Ammar et al.,
tldr: Realization of a Ramsey-type interferometer using a thermal cloud of magnetically trapped rubidium-87 atoms on an atom chip.
motivation: To demonstrate a compact, chip-based atom interferometer for precision measurements.
method: A thermal cloud of Rb-87 atoms is magnetically trapped on a chip, and a state-selective spatial splitting of internal states is used to realize a Ramsey interferometer.
result: The interferometer is successfully realized, showing interference fringes.
conclusion: Atom-chip interferometers can be built with thermal clouds, offering a compact platform for interferometry.

title: Increasing The Stability Of A Superfluid In A Rotating Necklace Potential
authors: Giulio Nesti And Luca Pezzè
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Nesti and Luca Pezzè

Recent experiments have probed the stability of ring superfluids in the presence of Josephson barriers or Gaussian impurities. Here we present a theoretical analysis that extends beyond the regimes explored so far. We study the onset of dynamical instabilities in a ring superfluid, addressing both t…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063326] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies dynamical instabilities in a ring superfluid with a rotating necklace potential, focusing on stability beyond previous regimes.
motivation: Recent experiments on ring superfluids with barriers or impurities motivate a theoretical analysis of stability in more general configurations.
method: The authors perform a theoretical analysis using a mean-field approach to study the onset of dynamical instabilities in a ring superfluid with a rotating necklace potential.
result: They find that the rotating necklace potential can increase the stability of the superfluid compared to static barriers, extending the regime of stable flow.
conclusion: The work provides insights into controlling superfluid stability using rotating potentials, relevant for ultracold atom experiments.

title: Gaussian Mode Coupling Of Spectrally Broadband Photons From Bulk Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion: A Spatial-spectral Mode Analysis Of Fiber Coupling
authors: Carlos Sevilla-Gutiérrez, Varun Raj Kaipalath, And Fabian Steinlechner
abstract:
Author(s): Carlos Sevilla-Gutiérrez, Varun Raj Kaipalath, and Fabian Steinlechner

Photon sources based on spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) are central to experimental quantum optics and quantum technologies. Their performance is commonly quantified by three metrics: pair-collection probability, heralding efficiency, and spectral purity. In bulk-crystal SPDC, these me…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063733] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the spatial-spectral mode coupling of broadband photons from bulk SPDC into single-mode fibers, focusing on optimizing pair-collection probability, heralding efficiency, and spectral purity.
motivation: Efficient fiber coupling of SPDC photons is crucial for quantum optics experiments and quantum technologies, but broadband photons from bulk crystals suffer from mode mismatch that degrades performance.
method: The authors develop a spatial-spectral mode analysis of the SPDC process, modeling the coupling of the down-converted fields into Gaussian fiber modes and computing the resulting joint spectral intensity and heralding efficiency.
result: They find that optimal fiber coupling requires balancing the phase-matching conditions and pump focusing to achieve high heralding efficiency and spectral purity simultaneously, with trade-offs quantified.
conclusion: The analysis provides design guidelines for SPDC sources to achieve high-performance fiber-coupled photon pairs, but the work is primarily an engineering optimization without fundamental quantum information or thermodynamic insights.

title: Bistable Fourth Sound Resonance In Superfluid $^{3}\mathrm{He}\text{−}\mathrm{B}$ Due To Gap Suppression
authors: Alexander J. Shook, Daksh Malhotra, Aymar Muhikira, And John P. Davis
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander J. Shook, Daksh Malhotra, Aymar Muhikira, and John P. Davis

Superfluidity in [MATH] exhibits many unique properties that are of interest to modern condensed matter research, including multiple superfluid phase transitions, topological defects, and exotic classes of excitations like Majorana and Weyl fermions. Many of the most interesting theoretic…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214519] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies bistable fourth sound resonance in superfluid 3He-B due to gap suppression, a condensed matter physics topic.
motivation: To understand nonlinear acoustic phenomena in superfluid 3He-B arising from order parameter suppression.
method: Experimental measurement of fourth sound resonance in a superfluid 3He-B cavity, analyzing nonlinear response and bistability.
result: Observation of bistable resonance behavior attributed to gap suppression by the sound field.
conclusion: The bistability provides insight into the nonlinear dynamics of superfluid 3He-B and its order parameter.

title: Many-body Wave Function And Edge Magnetization Of An Open $p+is$ Superconducting Chain
authors: Jiarui Jiao, Chao Xu, Congjun Wu, And Wang Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Jiao, Chao Xu, Congjun Wu, and Wang Yang

Although BCS wave functions for superconductors under periodic boundary conditions are well established, obtaining an explicit form of the many-body BCS wave function under open boundary condition is usually a nontrivial problem. In this work, we construct the exact BCS ground-state wave function of…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224525] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs the exact BCS ground-state wave function for an open p+is superconducting chain and studies its edge magnetization.
motivation: BCS wave functions under open boundary conditions are nontrivial but important for understanding edge properties of topological superconductors.
method: The authors derive the exact many-body wave function using a Bogoliubov transformation and solve the resulting BdG equations for the open chain.
result: They obtain an explicit form of the ground-state wave function and compute the edge magnetization, revealing topological edge modes.
conclusion: The work provides a rare exact solution for an open superconducting chain, clarifying the relationship between bulk topology and edge magnetism.

title: Large Anomalous Hall Conductivity And Topological Hall Effect In The Kagome Helimagnet ${\mathrm{MgMn}}_{6}{\mathrm{Ge}}_{6}$
authors: Jie Du, Zhonghua Ma, Hang Li, Xiaodong Zhou, Jie Chen, Tao Zhu, Yong-Chang Lau, And Wenhong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Du, Zhonghua Ma, Hang Li, Xiaodong Zhou, Jie Chen, Tao Zhu, Yong-Chang Lau, and Wenhong Wang

Magnetic kagome materials have emerged as a new platform for exploring exotic topological transport phenomena. The anomalous Hall effect, a phenomenon prevalently observed in various magnetic kagome materials, is commonly explained using Berry-curvature concepts. Here we report that ${}…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245146] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports large anomalous Hall conductivity and topological Hall effect in the kagome helimagnet MgMn6Ge6, attributed to Berry curvature from the non-coplanar spin texture.
motivation: To explore exotic topological transport phenomena in magnetic kagome materials, specifically the anomalous and topological Hall effects.
method: Synthesis of MgMn6Ge6 single crystals, measurement of Hall resistivity and magnetization, and analysis using Berry curvature concepts.
result: Observation of large anomalous Hall conductivity and a topological Hall effect arising from the non-coplanar spin structure.
conclusion: The kagome helimagnet MgMn6Ge6 is a promising platform for studying topological transport phenomena.

title: Strain-driven Antiferroelastic Switching Of Altermagnetism
authors: Fanjunjie Han, Shuaihao Tang, Jian-Dong Sun, Xin-Gang Zhao, And Haiyang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Fanjunjie Han, Shuaihao Tang, Jian-Dong Sun, Xin-Gang Zhao, and Haiyang Xu

Altermagnetism, characterized by pronounced momentum-space spin splitting without net magnetization, provides an emerging platform for spintronics. Yet nonvolatile control of its spin states remains a key challenge for device application. Here, we demonstrate that antiferroelastic lattice distortion…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214457] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates nonvolatile control of altermagnetism via antiferroelastic lattice distortion, enabling reversible switching of spin splitting without net magnetization.
motivation: Altermagnets offer spin splitting without net magnetization, but nonvolatile control of their spin states is needed for spintronic applications.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations to show that antiferroelastic strain can switch the altermagnetic order parameter in a model material.
result: They find that strain-driven antiferroelastic distortion reversibly flips the momentum-space spin splitting, providing a nonvolatile switching mechanism.
conclusion: This work establishes a pathway for electrically or mechanically controlling altermagnetic states, advancing altermagnet-based spintronics.

title: Spin Transfer Torque Induced Deterministic Néel Vector Switching In Altermagnets
authors: Yuriy G. Semenov And Ki Wook Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Yuriy G. Semenov and Ki Wook Kim

The process of spin-transfer torque in an altermagnet (AM) is theoretically investigated from the perspective of disparate effective exchange fields acting on the two sublattices. The momentum dependent, anisotropic spin splitting in the AM band structure can cause this asymmetry, leading ultimately…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224444] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically investigates spin-transfer torque in altermagnets, focusing on Néel vector switching driven by asymmetric exchange fields.
motivation: Altermagnets are a new class of magnetic materials with potential for spintronic applications; understanding spin-transfer torque in them is crucial for device development.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model based on momentum-dependent anisotropic spin splitting in the altermagnet band structure to compute spin-transfer torque and Néel vector dynamics.
result: They find that the asymmetric effective exchange fields on the two sublattices enable deterministic Néel vector switching via spin-transfer torque.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for using altermagnets in spintronic devices, but it is primarily a condensed matter physics result without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Predicting Interface And Spin States In Armchair Graphene Nanoribbon Junctions
authors: Sofia Sanz And Daniel Sánchez-Portal
abstract:
Author(s): Sofia Sanz and Daniel Sánchez-Portal

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235434] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical analysis of interface states in armchair graphene nanoribbon junctions.
motivation: Understanding interface states in graphene nanoribbon junctions is important for nanoelectronics, but the paper focuses on electronic structure rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Tight-binding or DFT calculations to predict interface states based on width combinations and junction geometries.
result: The number of interface states depends on more than just width differences, requiring detailed modeling.
conclusion: Predicting interface states in graphene nanoribbon junctions is nontrivial and requires beyond-simple considerations.

title: Loss/gain-induced Hall Effect Of Vortex Light
authors: Yucheng Lai, Yongliang Zhang, And Kai Chang
abstract:
Author(s): Yucheng Lai, Yongliang Zhang, and Kai Chang

The Hall effect provides a route for unidirectional manipulations of classical and quantum waves. In optics, the spin Hall effect (SHE) induced by the interaction between intrinsic angular momentum (AM) and material inhomogeneity enables AM-dependent control of light at the subwavelength scale. Desp…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245309] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports a loss/gain-induced Hall effect for vortex light in photonic systems, analogous to the spin Hall effect but for orbital angular momentum.
motivation: To explore how non-Hermitian effects (loss/gain) can induce a Hall-like effect for light carrying orbital angular momentum, extending the concept of the spin Hall effect to vortex beams.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a photonic system with loss/gain gradients and derive the equations of motion for vortex light, showing that the orbital angular momentum couples to the gradient, leading to transverse deflection.
result: They demonstrate that a loss/gain gradient induces a Hall effect for vortex light, where the direction of deflection depends on the sign of the orbital angular momentum, analogous to the spin Hall effect.
conclusion: This work reveals a new mechanism for controlling light with orbital angular momentum using non-Hermitian photonic structures, which may have applications in optical manipulation and information processing.

title: First-principles Prediction Of A Multiferroic Semiconductor With Switchable Spin-polarized Berry Curvature Dipole: ${\mathrm{PbMnO}}_{3}$:${\mathrm{PbVO}}_{3}$
authors: Arpita Paul And Umesh V. Waghmare

tldr: First-principles prediction of a multiferroic semiconductor with switchable spin-polarized Berry curvature dipole.
motivation: To discover new multiferroic materials with coexisting ferromagnetism, ferroelectricity, and Berry curvature dipole for potential applications in spintronics and optoelectronics.
method: First-principles density functional theory calculations and symmetry analysis of a PbMnO3/PbVO3 superlattice.
result: The superlattice exhibits multiferroicity with switchable spin-polarized Berry curvature dipole.
conclusion: The material is a promising candidate for multifunctional devices combining ferroelectric, ferromagnetic, and topological properties.

title: Collective Phonon Mixing And Eigenvector Transport Under Isotope Substitution
authors: Jeff Armstrong, Hamish Cavaye, Pankaj Sharma, And Matthew E. Potter
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Armstrong, Hamish Cavaye, Pankaj Sharma, and Matthew E. Potter

Isotopic substitution modifies nuclear masses without altering the electronic potential-energy surface to first order and is therefore often interpreted as a simple rescaling of vibrational frequencies. In solids with dense phonon manifolds, however, mass substitution acts as a parametric Hermitian …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214325] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how isotopic substitution affects phonon modes and eigenvector transport in solids, focusing on collective mixing and transport properties.
motivation: Isotopic substitution is often assumed to simply rescale vibrational frequencies, but in dense phonon manifolds it can cause more complex effects. The authors aim to understand these effects on phonon eigenvectors and transport.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and numerical simulations to analyze parametric Hermitian perturbations due to mass changes, studying eigenvector mixing and transport in phonon manifolds.
result: They find that isotopic substitution induces collective phonon mixing and modifies eigenvector transport, with implications for thermal conductivity and vibrational dynamics.
conclusion: Isotopic substitution in solids with dense phonon manifolds leads to nontrivial modifications of phonon eigenvectors and transport, beyond simple frequency rescaling.

title: Stacking Theory For Bilayer Two-dimensional Magnets
authors: Jun-Xi Du, Sike Zeng, And Yu-Jun Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Xi Du, Sike Zeng, and Yu-Jun Zhao

Two-dimensional unconventional magnetism has recently attracted growing interest due to its intriguing physical properties and promising applications in spintronics. However, existing studies on stacking-induced unconventional magnetism mainly focus on specific materials and stacking configurations.…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214455] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of stacking-induced unconventional magnetism in bilayer two-dimensional magnets, focusing on general principles rather than specific materials.
motivation: To understand how stacking configurations in bilayer 2D magnets can induce unconventional magnetic phases, beyond existing studies on specific materials.
method: Develops a stacking theory based on symmetry analysis and model Hamiltonians to classify possible magnetic states in bilayer systems.
result: Identifies general conditions for stacking-induced ferromagnetism, antiferromagnetism, and non-collinear magnetic orders.
conclusion: Provides a unified framework for predicting magnetic properties of bilayer 2D magnets based on stacking, guiding future material design.

title: Antiferromagnetic Solitons In NiO As Possible Entities For Logic Operations
authors: Z. Li, T. Chirac, J. Tranchida, J.-Y. Chauleau, And M. Viret

tldr: This paper studies antiferromagnetic solitons in NiO for potential logic operations, focusing on spin wave and domain wall propagation.
motivation: To explore antiferromagnetic materials as a platform for high-speed logic devices using solitons.
method: Atomistic simulations of NiO stripes to model spin wave and domain wall dynamics.
result: Demonstrates fast soliton velocities over 40 km/s and propagation properties that enable crossing and interference.
conclusion: Antiferromagnetic solitons in NiO show promise for logic operations, but the work is primarily materials and device physics without quantum information or thermodynamics connection.

title: Nontrivial Three-sublattice Magnetization In The Easy-axis Spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Xxz Antiferromagnet On The Triangular Lattice
authors: Masahiro Kadosawa, Masaaki Nakamura, Yukinori Ohta, And Satoshi Nishimoto

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224442] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the ground-state magnetic structure of an easy-axis spin-1/2 XXZ antiferromagnet on a triangular lattice using DMRG.
motivation: To understand nontrivial three-sublattice magnetization patterns in frustrated quantum magnets.
method: Density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) with spiral boundary conditions on finite clusters.
result: Identifies a nontrivial three-sublattice magnetic order in the easy-axis regime.
conclusion: The triangular lattice XXZ model exhibits rich magnetic phases beyond simple Néel order.

title: Spin-dependent Orbital Selectivity And Partial Kondo-like Screening In The Magnetically Ordered Hund's Metal ${\mathrm{Sr}}_{2}{\mathrm{CoO}}_{4}$
authors: Shivani Bhardwaj And Sudhir K. Pandey
abstract:
Author(s): Shivani Bhardwaj and Sudhir K. Pandey

Hund's metallicity in [MATH] transition metal oxides constitutes a rare class of compounds, since they have been long understood considering the dominance of Hubbard [MATH]. [MATH] belong to this rare class of metals; among them,…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235147] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-dependent orbital selectivity and Kondo-like screening in the Hund's metal Sr2CoO4 using DFT+DMFT.
motivation: To understand the electronic structure and correlation effects in Hund's metals, which are rare transition metal oxides with strong Hund's coupling.
method: First-principles DFT+DMFT calculations with continuous-time quantum Monte Carlo impurity solver.
result: They find spin-dependent orbital selectivity and partial Kondo-like screening in the magnetically ordered state.
conclusion: The study reveals complex interplay between Hund's coupling, orbital selectivity, and magnetic ordering in Sr2CoO4.

title: Orbital Hybridization Induces Giant Cubic Rashba Effect At The $\text{Cu/}{\mathrm{WO}}_{3}$ Interface
authors: Md Aktar Hossain And Saikat Das
abstract:
Author(s): Md Aktar Hossain and Saikat Das

Harnessing Rashba spin-orbit interaction and related spintronic functionalities has traditionally relied on metallic surfaces or interfaces containing elemental heavy metals. Here, using first-principles calculations and [MATH] as a model heterostructure, we…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235149] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the cubic Rashba effect at a Cu/WO3 interface using first-principles calculations, focusing on spintronic applications.
motivation: To explore orbital hybridization as a mechanism to induce a giant cubic Rashba effect without heavy elements, for spintronic devices.
method: First-principles density functional theory calculations on the Cu/WO3 heterostructure.
result: Orbital hybridization between Cu and WO3 leads to a large cubic Rashba spin splitting.
conclusion: The Cu/WO3 interface is a promising platform for spintronics based on the cubic Rashba effect.

title: Taxonomy Of Integrable And Ground-state Solvable Models: Jastrow Wave Functions On Graphs And Parent Hamiltonians
authors: Nilanjan Sasmal And Adolfo Del Campo
abstract:
Author(s): Nilanjan Sasmal and Adolfo del Campo

We introduce a family of many-body systems of distinguishable continuous-variable particles in which interparticle interactions are set by the adjacency matrix of a graph. The ground-state wave function of such systems is of a generalized Jastrow form involving the product of pair-correlation functi…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235151] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a family of many-body systems with Jastrow ground states on graphs, focusing on integrability and exact solvability.
motivation: To classify and construct exactly solvable many-body models with Jastrow wave functions, linking graph theory to quantum many-body physics.
method: The authors define a Hamiltonian based on the adjacency matrix of a graph, with interactions set by graph edges, and show that the ground state is a Jastrow product.
result: They provide a taxonomy of integrable and ground-state solvable models, demonstrating that the ground-state wave function is of generalized Jastrow form.
conclusion: The work offers a systematic way to generate exactly solvable models, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Toroidal Fermi Surface Geometry And Phonon-limited Transport In Nodal-line Semimetals
authors: Aman Anand And Alessandro de Martino
abstract:
Author(s): Aman Anand and Alessandro De Martino

Nodal-line semimetals (NLSs) can display unconventional quasiparticle dynamics and charge transport properties due to their extended band degeneracy and the peculiar geometry of their Fermi surface. We consider electron-acoustic phonon scattering as the dominant relaxation mechanism and compute the …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235432] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phonon-limited transport in nodal-line semimetals, focusing on the role of toroidal Fermi surface geometry.
motivation: Understanding charge transport in nodal-line semimetals is important for their potential applications, but the effect of Fermi surface geometry on transport has not been fully explored.
method: The authors compute the electrical resistivity due to electron-acoustic phonon scattering using Boltzmann transport theory, incorporating the toroidal Fermi surface geometry.
result: They find that the resistivity exhibits a distinct temperature dependence and anisotropy arising from the toroidal Fermi surface, differing from conventional metals.
conclusion: The toroidal Fermi surface geometry significantly influences phonon-limited transport in nodal-line semimetals, leading to unique transport signatures.

title: Free-electron Decoherence: Theory And Applications
authors: Cruz I. Velasco, Valerio Di Giulio, And F. Javier García de Abajo
abstract:
Author(s): Cruz I. Velasco, Valerio Di Giulio, and F. Javier García de Abajo

Electron microscopy relies on the spatial coherence of electron beams to generate atomic-scale images using interference and diffraction, which can be degraded by inelastic-scattering processes that induce decoherence. Here, we present a theoretical study of decoherence arising from the electromagne…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235433] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies decoherence of free electrons due to electromagnetic interactions, with applications in electron microscopy.
motivation: Understanding decoherence in electron beams is crucial for high-resolution electron microscopy, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on the electromagnetic interaction between the electron and its environment, likely using scattering theory or master equations.
result: They quantify decoherence rates and identify key factors affecting coherence, such as material properties and beam parameters.
conclusion: The work provides insights into decoherence mechanisms in electron microscopy but does not advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Theory Of ab Initio Downfolding With Arbitrary-range Electron-phonon Coupling
authors: Norm M. Tubman, Christopher J. N. Coveney, Chih-En Hsu, Andres Montoya-Castillo, Marina R. Filip, Jeffrey B. Neaton, Zhenglu Li, Vojtech Vlcek, And Antonios M. Alvertis
abstract:
Author(s): Norm M. Tubman, Christopher J. N. Coveney, Chih-En Hsu, Andres Montoya-Castillo, Marina R. Filip, Jeffrey B. Neaton, Zhenglu Li, Vojtech Vlcek, and Antonios M. Alvertis

Ab initio downfolding describes the electronic structure of materials within a low-energy subspace, often around the Fermi level. Typically starting from mean-field calculations, this framework allows for the calculation of one- and two-electron interactions, and the parametrization of a many-body H…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245144] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an ab initio downfolding method for electronic structure with arbitrary-range electron-phonon coupling.
motivation: To accurately describe low-energy electronic properties of materials by including long-range electron-phonon interactions beyond standard approximations.
method: The authors extend downfolding techniques to incorporate arbitrary-range electron-phonon coupling, starting from mean-field calculations and constructing effective Hamiltonians.
result: The method captures non-local electron-phonon effects that are important for polar materials and superconductors.
conclusion: The approach provides a systematic way to include long-range electron-phonon coupling in ab initio downfolding, improving accuracy for materials with strong electron-phonon interactions.

title: Emergence Of Multiple Zero Modes Bound To Vortices In Extended Topological Josephson Junctions
authors: Adrian Reich, Kiryl Piasotski, Eytan Grosfeld, And Alexander Shnirman

We study planar Josephson junctions formed on the surface of a three-dimensional topological insulator (Fu-Kane proposal). [Phys. Rev. B 113, 245426] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Majorana zero modes bound to vortices in topological Josephson junctions on a topological insulator surface.
motivation: To understand the emergence of multiple zero modes in extended topological Josephson junctions beyond the simplified one-dimensional model.
method: The authors analyze a planar Josephson junction on a 3D topological insulator, considering experimentally relevant parameter regimes and solving the effective Hamiltonian.
result: They find that multiple zero-energy Majorana modes can appear bound to vortices, depending on junction geometry and parameters.
conclusion: The work provides a more realistic description of Majorana modes in such junctions, relevant for topological quantum computing.

title: Spatiotemporal Migration Of Antiferromagnetic Domain Walls In ${\mathrm{Sr}}_{2}{\mathrm{IrO}}_{4}$
authors: Ian Robinson, David Yang, Ross Harder, Dina Sheyfer, Longlong Wu, Jack Griffiths, Emil Bozin, Mark P. M. title: Odd-parity Altermagnetism: A Spin Group Study
authors: Minghuan Zeng, Zheng Qin, Ling Qin, Shiping Feng, Lin Wu, Dong-Hui Xu, And Rui Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Minghuan Zeng, Zheng Qin, Ling Qin, Shiping Feng, Lin Wu, Dong-Hui Xu, and Rui Wang

Conventional altermagnetism, characterized by the even-parity spin splitting, has been intensively studied. Here, on the basis of spin-group analyses, the authors elucidate necessary conditions for the emergence of odd-parity altermagnetism. It is derived that the odd-parity altermagnetism arises from the following criteria: (i) the breaking nonmagnetic time reversal symmetry; (ii) the collinear compensated magnetism; (iii) the symmetry [C2||E¯] connecting opposite-spin sublattices, where ¯ respectively represent a 180° rotation around the axis perpendicular to spins and the inversion separating opposite-spin sublattices.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220412] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies odd-parity altermagnetism using spin group theory, focusing on symmetry conditions for spin splitting in collinear compensated magnets.
motivation: Conventional altermagnetism with even-parity spin splitting has been studied, but odd-parity altermagnetism remains unexplored. The authors aim to identify necessary symmetry conditions for its emergence.

conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for understanding odd-parity altermagnetism, which may have implications for spintronics and materials science, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

abstract:
