A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains shows they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations with potential relevance to low-dimensional magnetism.
method: Develops a nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons and analyzes their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
result: Chiral solitons appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and can be detected via inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical description of quantum chiral soliton dynamics and suggests experimental signatures.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To develop a non-perturbative method for studying strongly coupled conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using the fuzzy sphere as a regularization scheme.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry, to discretize the sphere and simulate fermionic CFTs, analyzing spectra and correlation functions.
result: They find evidence for emergent supersymmetry in the interacting fermionic CFTs and compute critical exponents and operator dimensions.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a viable numerical approach to study fermionic CFTs, revealing emergent supersymmetry and enabling future studies of strongly coupled theories.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures, focusing on magnetic phases in EuAg4Sb2.
motivation: To understand and control spin textures in moiré superlattices for potential information manipulation.
method: Neutron scattering and theoretical modeling to map spin textures and identify magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are revealed in EuAg4Sb2.
conclusion: Establishes a design framework for materials that manipulate information via spin-based vortex lattices.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the stability of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature using theoretical modeling.
motivation: To understand whether topological magnon gaps survive at finite temperatures, which is important for spintronic device applications.
method: Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures, likely using many-body perturbation theory or spin-wave theory.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point.
conclusion: The findings provide a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network, with implications for cryptography based on machine learning.
motivation: To understand whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational hardness of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network using algorithmic and complexity-theoretic tools.
result: Efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for designing cryptographic protocols based on machine learning models.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in complex networks is important but challenging; the authors aim to leverage physical principles to improve link prediction.
method: The framework integrates physical constraints (e.g., conservation laws, symmetries) into a machine learning model to infer causal links from time-series data.
result: The method outperforms standard causal inference techniques on several benchmark network dynamics datasets.
conclusion: Physics-informed approaches can enhance causal link prediction in networks, offering a new tool for analyzing complex systems.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anyon superfluidity of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers, focusing on topological criticality and exotic collective quantum states.
motivation: To understand and engineer exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers via topological criticality.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers, likely using field theory or topological arguments.
result: Topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids.
conclusion: The work offers a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall systems.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To understand the nature of the ground state and phase transition in the kagome ice compound HoAgGe, which exhibits spin ice behavior and potential hidden order.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements were performed on single crystals of HoAgGe, combined with neutron scattering and other techniques to characterize the magnetic properties and critical exponents.
result: The system undergoes a phase transition belonging to the three-dimensional XY universality class, and nonlinear susceptibility indicates hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground state.
conclusion: The study provides evidence for a novel ground state in kagome ice systems, with implications for frustrated magnetism and topological phases.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using ARPES.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but many are only stable at low temperatures; finding room-temperature flat bands is crucial for practical applications.
method: The authors synthesized layered transition-metal oxyhalides and performed angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to map the electronic band structure.
result: They observed intrinsic flat bands that are orbital-selective and remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for studying correlated electron states.
conclusion: These materials offer a promising platform for investigating strongly correlated physics and potential quantum phases at accessible temperatures.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses magneto-optical spectroscopy to probe quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, demonstrating electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To investigate the quantum anomalous Hall phase in twisted bilayer WSe2 and understand the interplay between topology and magnetism.
method: Magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, is used to probe the electronic structure and magnetic transitions.
result: Observation of a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field control over transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer WSe2 is a promising platform for studying topological phases with tunable magnetism.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in soft condensed matter physics with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Hyperuniform fluids exhibit suppressed density fluctuations at large scales, and their critical behavior at the liquid-vapor transition is of fundamental interest in statistical mechanics.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to characterize the critical exponents and scaling behavior of hyperuniform fluids near the liquid-gas critical point.
result: Hyperuniform fluids show unusual calmness yet high susceptibility at the critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
conclusion: The findings reveal novel critical phenomena in hyperuniform systems, relevant to soft matter physics but not to the user's research directions.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates ballistic spin transport and spin valve effect in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing, a purely condensed matter physics result with no quantum information or thermodynamics angle.
motivation: To realize coherent spin control in graphene via electron optics, enabling gate-tunable spin transport.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene heterostructures, measuring spin-dependent electron trajectories.
result: Observation of ballistic spin transport and a spin valve effect, with gate-tunable spin coherence.
conclusion: Graphene can serve as a platform for spin-based electron optics, but the work is focused on spintronics and condensed matter, not quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum algorithm for computing persistence in topological data analysis, claiming exponential speedup.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a powerful tool for extracting features from data, but classical algorithms are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and sampling techniques to compute persistence diagrams more efficiently.
result: They prove a provable exponential quantum speedup over classical algorithms for certain instances of the problem.
conclusion: This work suggests that quantum computers could enable practical applications in topological data analysis, though practical implementation remains challenging.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A high-level perspective piece proposing a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, focusing on scientific milestones rather than technical results.
motivation: To outline a roadmap for bridging the gap between theoretical quantum computing and practical applications.
method: Conceptual framework based on expert opinion and analysis of current quantum computing progress.
result: A five-stage framework detailing milestones for quantum utility.
conclusion: The framework provides a structured path but does not present new technical contributions.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, serving as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, and its approximation is a candidate for quantum advantage.
method: The authors design an end-to-end quantum algorithm that maps the Jones polynomial evaluation to a quantum circuit, using techniques from topological quantum computing and implementing it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They demonstrate the algorithm on a trapped-ion quantum computer, showing that the quantum algorithm can approximate the Jones polynomial for certain inputs, and discuss the resource requirements and potential for quantum advantage.
conclusion: The work provides a practical benchmark for quantum computers and suggests that the Jones polynomial approximation may be a viable candidate for demonstrating quantum advantage in the near term.

title: Photon Catalysis For General Multimode Multi-Photon Quantum State Preparation
authors: Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, And Massimo Frigerio
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, and Massimo Frigerio

Using a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition, every photonic state can be prepared with realistic experimental tools and a predictable number of steps.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020323] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing arbitrary photonic states using symmetric tensor decomposition and photon catalysis.
motivation: To provide a systematic and experimentally feasible approach for generating complex multimode multi-photon quantum states.
method: The authors use symmetric tensor decomposition to express any photonic state as a linear combination of simpler states, then employ photon catalysis (adding and subtracting photons) to realize the decomposition experimentally.
result: They show that any photonic state can be prepared with a predictable number of steps using realistic experimental tools.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a universal and efficient recipe for photonic state preparation, advancing quantum optics experiments.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, covering HHL and post-HHL developments.
motivation: Linear system solving is a central task in computation, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup for certain problems.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, block-encoding, quantum signal processing, and variable-time amplitude amplification.
result: It provides a taxonomy of QLSP algorithms, discusses their complexity, and surveys applications in machine learning, differential equations, and data fitting.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource requirements and input model assumptions.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge in 2D magnetism, which has revealed new phenomena and challenged established theories.
method: The paper is a review that surveys experimental and theoretical progress in 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The review covers ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and magneto-optical interactions.
conclusion: The field is rapidly evolving with expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and application prospects.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from geometric frustration and interference effects.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic states including unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism, and electronic nematicity, driven by frustration and interference.
conclusion: Kagome metals provide a rich platform for exploring correlated electron physics and may lead to new quantum states.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: Spin glasses are a model system for complex disordered systems, and understanding their dynamics has broad applications.
method: The review synthesizes experimental results, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations.
result: Highlights the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation in advancing the field.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich area for future research, with implications for many physical systems.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on material candidates and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in candidate materials, discussing their magnetic properties and topological signatures.
result: Highlights key materials such as α-RuCl3 and their chiral edge modes, but does not present new experimental or theoretical results.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of research with promising candidates, but definitive experimental confirmation is still lacking.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to neural network data, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a central challenge in neuroscience, and statistical physics offers tools to model such systems.
method: The authors review recent work using maximum entropy models and renormalization group analysis on recordings from thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural populations, demonstrating that statistical physics principles can predict neural activity.
conclusion: Statistical mechanics provides a powerful framework for analyzing neural network data, bridging theory and experiment in neuroscience.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: To survey quantum-mechanical aspects of magnetic skyrmions, including interactions underlying their formation and their own quantum features.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on skyrmions, covering topological field theory, spin textures, and quantum effects.
result: Summarizes current understanding of skyrmion quantum properties and their potential for spintronic and quantum technologies.
conclusion: Magnetic skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior that may enable novel functionalities, but the field is still developing.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium reviewing synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries such as fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in exotic geometries that enable simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical implementations in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems.
result: Summarizes progress in realizing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher-dimensional systems.
conclusion: These synthetic systems offer new platforms for studying quantum physics beyond standard geometries.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of using massive quantum systems to probe gravity, including tests of quantum gravity effects and entanglement mediation.
motivation: To understand the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, which is poorly understood, by using massive quantum systems as probes.
method: Review of theoretical proposals and experimental efforts, including matter-wave interferometry, optomechanics, and tests of gravity-induced entanglement.
result: Summarizes current theoretical models and experimental progress, highlighting that no definitive evidence of quantum gravity has been found yet.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to test quantum gravity, but further theoretical and experimental work is needed.

title: Real-Space Dynamic Electron Correlation In Beryllium
authors: Rudra B. Bista, Yuya Shinohara, Wojciech Dmowski, Chae Woo Ryu, Jung Ho Kim, Mary Upton, Hlynur Gretarsson, Martin Sundermann, And Takeshi Egami
abstract:
Author(s): Rudra B. Bista, Yuya Shinohara, Wojciech Dmowski, Chae Woo Ryu, Jung Ho Kim, Mary Upton, Hlynur Gretarsson, Martin Sundermann, and Takeshi Egami

The size of the exchange-correlation hole in beryllium is about 2 Å, but it extends up to about 5 Å at the plasmon excitation energy, demonstrating that electron correlations are affected significantly by electron dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256402] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies real-space dynamic electron correlation in beryllium using inelastic X-ray scattering, focusing on the size of the exchange-correlation hole at plasmon excitation energies.
motivation: Understanding electron correlations in materials is fundamental to condensed matter physics, but this work is purely experimental and materials-focused without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use inelastic X-ray scattering to measure the dynamic structure factor of beryllium and extract the real-space exchange-correlation hole size.
result: The exchange-correlation hole size is about 2 Å at low energy but extends to about 5 Å at the plasmon excitation energy, showing significant dynamic effects.
conclusion: Electron correlations in beryllium are strongly influenced by electron dynamics, as evidenced by the energy-dependent size of the exchange-correlation hole.

title: Fluid Flow And Spatiotemporal Chaos In Chemically Active Emulsions
authors: Charu Datt, Jonathan Bauermann, Nazmi Burak Budanur, And Frank Jülicher
abstract:
Author(s): Charu Datt, Jonathan Bauermann, Nazmi Burak Budanur, and Frank Jülicher

We study phase-separating fluid mixtures as they demix in the presence of chemical reactions that maintain them away from thermodynamic equilibrium. We show that in such chemically active emulsions the interplay of chemical reactions, phase separation, and hydrodynamics effects complex self-organiza…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 254001] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fluid flow and spatiotemporal chaos in chemically active emulsions, focusing on non-equilibrium phase separation and hydrodynamics.
motivation: To understand how chemical reactions and phase separation interact with hydrodynamics to produce complex self-organization in active emulsions.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model combining Cahn-Hilliard phase separation, chemical reactions, and Navier-Stokes hydrodynamics, and analyze it numerically.
result: They find that chemical activity can drive spatiotemporal chaos and complex fluid flows, with patterns depending on reaction rates and system parameters.
conclusion: Chemically active emulsions exhibit rich non-equilibrium dynamics that could be relevant for active matter and biological systems.

title: Block-Type Antiferromagnetism In Single Chain Quasi-One-Dimensional ${\mathrm{K}}_{3}{\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}{\mathrm{Se}}_{4}$
authors: Fei Gao, Nikhil Dhale, Ling-Fang Lin, Keith M. Taddei, Yang Zhang, Clarina Dela Cruz, Elbio Dagotto, And Bing Lv
abstract:

One-dimensional (1D) structures provide a unique platform to study the correlated quantum interactions and phase transitions such as unconventional magnetism and superconducting states. Here, we report that iron chalcogenide [MATH] exhibits an unusual bl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256706] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports an unusual block-type antiferromagnetic order in a quasi-one-dimensional iron chalcogenide, studied via neutron scattering and first-principles calculations.
motivation: To understand the magnetic structure and phase transitions in low-dimensional iron chalcogenides, which may host unconventional magnetism.
method: Single-crystal neutron diffraction and density functional theory (DFT) calculations were used to determine the magnetic ground state.
result: The material exhibits a block-type antiferromagnetic order with ferromagnetically coupled Fe dimers arranged antiferromagnetically along the chain.
conclusion: The discovery of this magnetic order provides insight into the interplay of spin, charge, and lattice in low-dimensional systems.

title: Critical Phenomenon Inside Asymptotically Flat Black Holes With Spontaneous Scalarization
authors: Li Li, Ze Sun, And Fu-Guo Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Li Li, Ze Sun, and Fu-Guo Yang

We study the nonlinear interior dynamics of spontaneously scalarized black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory with zero cosmological constant, revealing novel critical phenomena. We demonstrate that, for a wide range of scalar-electromagnetic couplings, scalarized black holes possess no smooth …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251402] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies critical phenomena inside spontaneously scalarized black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory.
motivation: To understand the nonlinear interior dynamics and critical behavior of scalarized black holes beyond general relativity.
method: Numerical simulations of the Einstein-Maxwell-scalar field equations with zero cosmological constant.
result: Discovery of novel critical phenomena for a wide range of scalar-electromagnetic couplings, including the absence of smooth interior solutions.
conclusion: Scalarized black holes exhibit rich interior dynamics with critical phenomena, extending our understanding of black hole interiors.

title: Ultrafast Three-dimensional Steering Of Electronic Ring Currents In Benzene: Coherent Control Of Angular Momentum
authors: Dongming Jia, Yuteng Zhou, Chunmei Liu, And Yonggang Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Dongming Jia, Yuteng Zhou, Chunmei Liu, and Yonggang Yang

Coherent control of electronic ring currents enables the steering of optomagnetic responses on femtosecond timescales. However, most existing schemes confine these currents to the molecular plane, effectively constraining the electronic angular momentum (EAM) vector to a fixed direction. Here, we de…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063115] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates ultrafast coherent control of electronic ring currents in benzene to steer the electronic angular momentum vector in three dimensions.
motivation: Existing schemes confine ring currents to the molecular plane, limiting control of the angular momentum direction; the authors aim to achieve full 3D steering.
method: Using shaped femtosecond laser pulses with tailored polarization and phase, they excite specific superpositions of electronic states in benzene to induce and control ring currents.
result: They show that the electronic angular momentum vector can be rotated out of the molecular plane, enabling three-dimensional control on femtosecond timescales.
conclusion: This work extends coherent control of molecular ring currents to three dimensions, with potential applications in ultrafast optomagnetic devices.

title: Two-color Laser Cooling With The Rubidium Optical Clock Transition
authors: Wictor C. Magno And Flavio C. Cruz
abstract:
Author(s): Wictor C. Magno and Flavio C. Cruz

The three-level [MATH] cascade transition of [MATH] is widely used as a reference for optical frequency standards based on two-photon spectroscopy, implemented with either single-color excitation at 778 nm or two-color excitation at 780 and 776 n…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063114] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a two-color laser cooling scheme using the rubidium optical clock transition.
motivation: Laser cooling is essential for quantum sensors and atomic clocks, but standard cooling methods may not be optimal for all transitions.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a two-color cooling scheme on the 5S-5D two-photon transition in rubidium, using rate equations and Doppler cooling theory.
result: They find that two-color cooling can achieve lower temperatures than single-color cooling for this transition, with potential for sub-Doppler temperatures.
conclusion: Two-color laser cooling on the rubidium optical clock transition is a viable technique for improving atomic clock performance.

title: Scattering Symmetries In Diffraction Gratings
authors: Karim Achouri
abstract:
Author(s): Karim Achouri

Metasurfaces enable powerful control of electromagnetic waves using subwavelength planar structures, but their deeply subwavelength periodicity typically suppresses propagating diffraction orders, which limits the number of available scattering channels. Diffraction gratings and metagratings overcom…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063528] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies scattering symmetries in diffraction gratings and metagratings, focusing on electromagnetic wave control.
motivation: To understand and exploit scattering symmetries in diffraction gratings for advanced wave manipulation.
method: Theoretical analysis of scattering symmetries using group theory and electromagnetic theory.
result: Identifies constraints and opportunities for controlling diffraction orders via symmetry.
conclusion: Symmetry principles can guide the design of metagratings with desired scattering properties.

title: Resolution Of The Hyperfine Puzzle And Its Significance For Two-fermion Dirac Atoms
authors: Gordon Baym And Glennys R. Farrar
abstract:
Author(s): Gordon Baym and Glennys R. Farrar

If we could shrink the ground-state wave function of a hydrogen atom to a size [MATH], at fixed electron mass and charge, the singlet hyperfine attraction in a spin singlet state would scale as [MATH]—faster than the increase in kinetic energy—raising the question of why the hyperfine interaction …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062219] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper resolves a puzzle in the hyperfine structure of two-fermion Dirac atoms, focusing on the scaling of hyperfine attraction in hydrogen-like systems.
motivation: To understand why the hyperfine interaction does not cause collapse in hydrogen atoms despite its rapid scaling with wavefunction compression.
method: Analytical calculations using Dirac equation and relativistic quantum mechanics for two-fermion systems.
result: The hyperfine puzzle is resolved by showing that relativistic effects prevent collapse, consistent with known physics.
conclusion: The work clarifies a long-standing theoretical issue in atomic physics but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Vibrational And Diffusional Thermal Transport In Amorphous And Deeply Supercooled Liquid Alumina
authors: Honggang Zhang, Xiaoyi Chen, Yangshun Lan, Changchun Ding, Dingbo Zhang, Yuxiang Ni, And Hua Bao
abstract:
Author(s): Honggang Zhang, Xiaoyi Chen, Yangshun Lan, Changchun Ding, Dingbo Zhang, Yuxiang Ni, and Hua Bao

Thermal transport in amorphous materials involves a complex interplay between anharmonicity and atomic-scale dynamics, particularly across the glass transition. To elucidate the underlying mechanisms, we investigate the temperature dependence of thermal transport in amorphous ${}_{2}{\mat…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224318] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies thermal transport in amorphous and supercooled liquid alumina, focusing on vibrational and diffusional contributions.
motivation: Understanding thermal transport in amorphous materials is important for applications like thermal barrier coatings, but the mechanisms across the glass transition are not fully understood.
method: The authors use molecular dynamics simulations to compute thermal conductivity and analyze the contributions from vibrational (phonon-like) and diffusional (atomic motion) channels.
result: They find that thermal conductivity decreases with temperature in the amorphous phase and increases in the supercooled liquid, with diffusional transport becoming dominant near the glass transition.
conclusion: The study elucidates the crossover from vibrational to diffusional thermal transport in alumina, providing insights into heat conduction in disordered systems.

title: Strongly Quenched Kramers Doublet Magnetism In ${\mathrm{SmMgAl}}_{11}{\mathrm{O}}_{19}$
authors: Sonu Kumar, Barbora Salajová, Andrej Kancko, Cinthia A. Corrêa, Shuvajit Halder, And Ross H. Colman
abstract:

We report magnetic susceptibility, isothermal magnetization, and specific-heat measurements on the rare-earth hexaaluminate [MATH], where [MATH] realizes a strongly quenched Kramers doublet on a triangular lattice with an exceptionally weak net exchan…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224443] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports magnetic susceptibility, magnetization, and specific-heat measurements on a rare-earth hexaaluminate compound with a strongly quenched Kramers doublet on a triangular lattice.
motivation: To understand the magnetic properties of SmMgAl11O19, a rare-earth hexaaluminate with a triangular lattice and strongly quenched Kramers doublet.
method: Experimental measurements of magnetic susceptibility, isothermal magnetization, and specific heat.
result: Observation of a strongly quenched Kramers doublet with exceptionally weak net exchange interactions.
conclusion: The compound exhibits interesting low-temperature magnetism but is not directly relevant to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Auxiliary Field Quantum Monte Carlo At The Basis Set Limit: Application To Lattice Constants
authors: Moritz Humer, Martin Schlipf, Zoran Sukurma, Sajad Bazrafshan, And Georg Kresse
abstract:
Author(s): Moritz Humer, Martin Schlipf, Zoran Sukurma, Sajad Bazrafshan, and Georg Kresse

We present a plane-wave (PW) implementation of the auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) method within the projector augmented-wave (PAW) formalism in the Vienna ab initio Simulation Package (VASP). By employing an exact inversion of the PAW overlap operator, our approach maintains cubic scali…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235146] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a plane-wave implementation of auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo for computing lattice constants of solids.
motivation: Accurate computation of lattice constants is important for materials science, and AFQMC offers high accuracy but is typically limited to small basis sets.
method: The authors implement AFQMC within the PAW formalism in VASP, using exact inversion of the PAW overlap operator to maintain cubic scaling and enable plane-wave basis sets.
result: The method achieves basis-set limit accuracy for lattice constants of various solids, demonstrating systematic convergence and agreement with experiment.
conclusion: The plane-wave AFQMC approach provides a practical and accurate method for computing lattice constants and other ground-state properties of solids.

title: Quasiparticle Interference In LiFeAs: Signature Of Inelastic Tunneling Through Spin Fluctuations
authors: Shun Chi, Carolina A. Marques, W. N. Hardy, Ruixing Liang, Pinder Dosanjh, D. A. Bonn, S. A. Burke, And Peter Wahl
abstract:
Author(s): Shun Chi, Carolina A. Marques, W. N. Hardy, Ruixing Liang, Pinder Dosanjh, D. A. Bonn, S. A. Burke, and Peter Wahl

Quasiparticle interference (QPI) is a powerful tool to characterize the symmetry of the superconducting order parameter in unconventional superconductors, by mapping the spatial dependence of elastic tunneling of electrons between the tip of a scanning tunneling microscope and a sample. Here, we con…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235148] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quasiparticle interference in the iron-based superconductor LiFeAs, attributing it to inelastic tunneling via spin fluctuations rather than elastic scattering.
motivation: Understanding the pairing mechanism in unconventional superconductors like LiFeAs is crucial; quasiparticle interference (QPI) can reveal the symmetry of the superconducting order parameter.
method: The authors use scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) to measure QPI patterns and compare them with theoretical simulations that include both elastic and inelastic tunneling channels mediated by spin fluctuations.
result: They find that the observed QPI patterns are best explained by inelastic tunneling through spin fluctuations, not by elastic scattering from impurities, indicating the importance of spin fluctuations in the pairing.
conclusion: The work provides evidence that spin fluctuations play a key role in the superconducting pairing of LiFeAs, advancing the understanding of iron-based superconductors.

title: Pressure-lifted Néel Temperature In The Van Der Waals Antiferromagnet $\mathrm{Mn}\mathrm{P}{\mathrm{S}}_{3}$
authors: Hongze Zhao, Zeyu Li, Xiangqi Wang, Xiaoyu Sun, Zilong Xu, Di Mai, Chong Zhong, Yang Zhang, He Wang, Rucheng Dai, Zhongping Wang, Zhenhua Qiao, And Zengming Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Hongze Zhao, Zeyu Li, Xiangqi Wang, Xiaoyu Sun, Zilong Xu, Di Mai, Chong Zhong, Yang Zhang, He Wang, Rucheng Dai, Zhongping Wang, Zhenhua Qiao, and Zengming Zhang

Two-dimensional magnetic materials have emerged as a frontier in condensed matter physics, offering a versatile platform for investigating unprecedented quantum phenomena under extreme conditions. This work focuses on [MATH], a prototypical Heisenberg antiferromagnet…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214454] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the pressure dependence of the Néel temperature in the van der Waals antiferromagnet MnPS3, a condensed matter physics topic without direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand how hydrostatic pressure affects magnetic ordering in two-dimensional magnetic materials, which are of interest for fundamental physics and potential spintronic applications.
method: Single-crystal X-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy under high pressure, combined with first-principles calculations to analyze structural and magnetic changes.
result: The Néel temperature increases with pressure up to ~2.5 GPa, then decreases; this is attributed to pressure-induced changes in interlayer coupling and magnetic anisotropy.
conclusion: Pressure can tune magnetic properties in van der Waals antiferromagnets, but the system remains a classical magnet without quantum information or thermodynamic relevance.

title: Selective Wave Transmission In Strongly Nonlinear Disordered Granular Chains
authors: João Guilherme Pinto de Freitas, Luis Paulo Silveira Machado, And Surajit Sen
abstract:
Author(s): João Guilherme Pinto de Freitas, Luis Paulo Silveira Machado, and Surajit Sen

Chains of 1000 granules in mutual contact, without precompression, and with random radii that follow a normal distribution are studied numerically. The standard deviation [MATH] controls the disorder level. The chains are subject to (i) a striker impact and (ii) an actuator that imposes band-limited wh…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065426] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Numerical study of wave transmission in disordered granular chains under nonlinear conditions.
motivation: To understand how disorder affects wave propagation in strongly nonlinear granular systems, which is relevant for impact mitigation and energy harvesting.
method: Simulated chains of 1000 granules with random radii (normal distribution) under striker impact and band-limited white noise actuation, varying disorder strength.
result: Disorder leads to selective wave transmission, with certain frequency components being filtered or localized depending on disorder level.
conclusion: Disorder can be used to control wave propagation in granular chains, offering potential for designing mechanical filters or shock absorbers.

title: First-passage Processes In A Deterministic One-dimensional Cellular Automaton Model Of Traffic Flow
authors: Ofer Biham, Gilad Hertzberg Rabinovich, And Eytan Katzav
abstract:
Author(s): Ofer Biham, Gilad Hertzberg Rabinovich, and Eytan Katzav

We present analytical results for first-passage processes in a deterministic one-dimensional cellular automaton (CA) model of traffic flow. Starting at time [MATH] from a random initial state with car density [MATH], at every time step [MATH] each car moves one step to the right if the cell on its right …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064145] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Analytical results for first-passage processes in a deterministic one-dimensional cellular automaton model of traffic flow.
motivation: To understand first-passage statistics in a simple traffic flow model, which may have implications for transport and jamming phenomena.
method: Analytical calculations using the deterministic cellular automaton rule 184 and combinatorial methods to compute first-passage time distributions.
result: Exact expressions for the first-passage time distribution and its moments are derived for various car densities.
conclusion: The model provides a tractable example of first-passage processes in deterministic many-particle systems, but the results are specific to traffic flow and not directly applicable to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Stochastic Search With Space-dependent Diffusivity
authors: Hwai-Ray Tung And Sean D. Lawley
abstract:
Author(s): Hwai-Ray Tung and Sean D. Lawley

The canonical model of stochastic search tracks a randomly diffusing “searcher” until it finds a “target.” Owing to its many applications across science and engineering, this perennially popular problem has been thoroughly investigated in a variety of models. However, aside from some exactly solvabl…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064149] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A study of stochastic search with space-dependent diffusivity, analyzing mean first passage times and search efficiency.
motivation: To understand how spatially varying diffusivity affects the efficiency of random search processes, which has applications in biology and engineering.
method: Analytical and numerical methods for solving the diffusion equation with space-dependent diffusion coefficient, computing mean first passage times.
result: Derived expressions for mean first passage time and search probability, showing that space-dependent diffusivity can significantly alter search efficiency compared to constant diffusivity.
conclusion: Space-dependent diffusivity is a crucial factor in stochastic search problems and can be exploited to optimize search strategies.

title: Collective Decision Making With Higher-order Interactions On $d$-uniform Hypergraphs

[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064311] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies opinion dynamics on d-uniform hypergraphs, focusing on collective decision making with higher-order interactions.
motivation: Understanding how group interactions influence opinion dynamics is fundamental to collective behavior, and higher-order structures may reveal new phenomena.
method: The authors propose a model of opinion dynamics on d-uniform hypergraphs and analyze it using analytical and numerical methods.
result: The model shows that higher-order interactions can lead to consensus or polarization depending on parameters.
conclusion: Higher-order interactions significantly affect opinion dynamics, and hypergraph models capture these effects better than pairwise networks.

title: Collective Ballistic Motion Explains Fast Aggregation In Adhesive Active Matter

tldr: This paper studies ballistic aggregation in active matter systems of self-aligning adhesive particles, focusing on collective motion and clustering kinetics.
motivation: Understanding fast aggregation in active matter, inspired by motile cells in tissue formation.
method: Simulations of self-aligning adhesive particles, analyzing cluster persistence length and intercluster distance scaling.
result: A flocking transition leads to ballistic aggregation where cluster persistence length grows faster with mass than intercluster distance.
conclusion: Collective ballistic motion explains rapid aggregation in adhesive active matter systems.

title: Dynamic Monte Carlo Study Of Rigidity Percolation Using An Event-based Ensemble Approach

tldr: This paper studies rigidity percolation dynamics on a triangular lattice using an event-based ensemble Monte Carlo method.
motivation: Understanding the onset of mechanical stability in disordered materials is important, but the dynamics of rigidity transitions have been less studied than static properties.
method: The authors employ an event-based ensemble approach to simulate the dynamic Monte Carlo process of rigidity percolation on a triangular lattice.
result: They characterize the dynamic rigidity transition and extract critical exponents.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the dynamic aspects of rigidity percolation, but it is purely classical statistical mechanics with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Relations Among Different Inequality Measures In Complex Systems: From Kinetic Exchange To Earthquake Models

[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064308] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper numerically studies inequality measures in kinetic wealth-exchange and earthquake models, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand inequality distributions in complex systems such as wealth exchange and earthquakes.
method: Numerical simulations of two kinetic wealth-exchange models and two earthquake models, computing various inequality measures.
result: Quantitative comparisons of inequality measures across the different models.
conclusion: The study provides insights into inequality patterns in complex systems but does not relate to the user's research interests.

title: Emergence Of A Fluctuation-driven Cooperative Solidlike Phase In Potts Model Monolayers

[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064410] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fluctuation-driven cooperative solidlike phases in cellular Potts model monolayers, focusing on biological cell dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how variations in CPM simulation implementations affect observed phase transitions and structural ordering in cell monolayers.
method: Cellular Potts model simulations with different definitions of cell perimeter and area constraints, analyzing dynamics and phase behavior.
result: A fluctuation-driven cooperative solidlike phase emerges under certain simulation conditions, distinct from conventional liquid or solid phases.
conclusion: The choice of simulation implementation significantly impacts the observed phase behavior, highlighting the need for standardization in CPM studies.

title: Second-order Modified Mean-field Theory For Textured Immobilized Magnetic Nanoparticles

result: The theory provides improved predictions for magnetization curves and susceptibility compared to first-order theories.
conclusion: The second-order theory is a valuable tool for understanding magnetic properties of textured nanoparticle systems.

title: Discontinuous Wealth-gradient Transition Driving Cooperation
authors: Hyun Gyu Lee, Hyeong-Chai Jeong, And Deok-Sun Lee
abstract:

The universal prevalence of cooperation is puzzling, as defection typically yields higher payoffs than cooperation, motivating searches for hidden pathways to cooperation. Here we study a game-theoretic model on a lattice structured population in which interaction payoffs are scaled by the minimum o…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064306] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cooperation in a game-theoretic model on a lattice, focusing on wealth gradients and phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the emergence of cooperation despite the payoff advantage of defection is a classic puzzle in evolutionary game theory.

title: Spatial Correlations In Susceptible-infected-susceptible Processes On Random Regular Graphs
authors: Alexander Leibenzon, Samuel W. S. Johnson, Ruth E. Baker, And Michael Assaf

In network-based susceptible-infected-susceptible (SIS) models of infectious disease transmission, infection can only occur between directly connected individuals. [Phys. Rev. E 113, 064307] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spatial correlations in SIS epidemic models on random regular graphs using pair approximation and Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: Understanding how network structure induces spatial correlations in epidemic spread is important for accurate modeling of infectious diseases.

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: A review of the Wannier-function software ecosystem for materials simulations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the methods and tools based on Wannier functions for electronic structure calculations.
method: The paper reviews the theory of Wannier functions and describes the interoperable software ecosystem, including codes for maximally localized Wannier functions and their applications.
result: The review catalogs the capabilities and interconnections of various software packages in the Wannier-function ecosystem.
conclusion: The Wannier-function ecosystem is a major instrument for the electronic-structure community, enabling accurate and insightful materials simulations.
